original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
In the bIsStreamFile == FALSE fallback path, the SIZE branch uses the requested listIndex to read a fileDescriptor element and dereference its file-size field; the RANGE branch uses the same index to read a file_names element as an argument to the file-content reader. If the index exceeds the valid range of the corresponding array, the read is out of bounds and an invalid pointer may be used afterward. Existing context, fileContentsRequest, clipboard non-null checks, allocation-success check, and OLE-result check do not constrain the index; allocating an output buffer of sizeof(UINT64) in the SIZE branch also cannot protect source-array access.

original_descriptions.security_change:

Current review fix mechanism description: After a requested index enters each array branch that actually uses it, and before the first subscript access, enforce a strict upper bound using the shared count of valid elements; reject index >= count and exit through existing error cleanup rather than checking only after reading an element.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The RMF_PAD branch first validates the padding area, advances ap by padlen, recomputes rhp, and then directly reads sh_flags at the new position with EXTRACT_LE_8BITS. The preceding field check concerns the old rhp, and the padding-area check does not guarantee that the post-padding flags field is readable. When the padding is still within the capture range but the new flags field is truncated, the read may go out of bounds. The comparison between length and padlen constrains packet length but cannot replace a capture-boundary check for the new field.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read: route-flag field's capture boundary is not revalidated after skipping padding
original_descriptions.security_change:
After advancing ap, subtracting length, and recomputing rhp, add ND_TCHECK(rhp->rh_short.sh_flags) before extracting the new sh_flags, so the boundary check and actual read use the same relocated field. Under ND_TCHECK's boundary-check and failed-truncation semantics, an unreadable field enters truncation handling before extraction.
Current review fix mechanism description: After a parse cursor moves, validation of the old position or skipped range cannot be reused for the new object; recompute the target address, validate the field about to be read, and only then extract and use its value.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: both sides clearly show a local fix for a post-relocation field read in the same padding branch. This assumes ND_TCHECK performs capture-boundary validation and stops the later read on failure; its macro definition is not provided, so all length calculations and downstream parsing in after are not established safe.

When path points to a valid empty string, strlen(path) is 0 and path_len - 1 is -1. The old code first reads path[-1] while testing whether the last character is a path separator; if path points to the start of a character array, that read crosses the lower bound. Both original character comparisons rely on the same indexed read and cannot protect the empty-string boundary.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read caused by an empty string and negative index
original_descriptions.security_change:
Before both last-character reads, add path_len > 0. Through && short-circuit evaluation, when path_len is 0 the code no longer computes or accesses path[path_len - 1] and directly returns MZ_OK; for a positive length it retains the original last-character tests.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before accessing the last element with length minus one, verify that the length is positive and use short-circuit evaluation so the length condition executes before index calculation and read; a zero-length path bypasses last-element access.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the complete source confirms a local fix relationship between empty-string negative-index access and the preceding length condition, without needing to prove attack reachability. The conclusion assumes path is a valid string that strlen can read; lower-bound crossing additionally assumes path points to the array start. after still does not handle invalid or null pointers and does not verify that the strlen result fits in int32_t, so all inputs are not claimed safe.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
tmpName is allocated for to_read bytes, and i scans for the first zero byte. If to_read > 0 and all of those bytes are nonzero, i increments to to_read; the old condition reads tmpName[i] first and checks i < to_read only afterward, so it reads one byte beyond the buffer end. The post-loop i == to_read check can reject the data but cannot prevent the out-of-bounds read that already occurred.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): the loop condition accesses the buffer before validating the index boundary
original_descriptions.security_change:
The only change is to swap the two && operands. after checks i < to_read first and reads tmpName[i] only when it holds; at the boundary, short-circuit evaluation stops the scan, after which the existing branch frees tmpName and returns GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE.
Current review fix mechanism description: For a sentinel scan over a bounded buffer, place the index-boundary check before dereference and use short-circuit evaluation so every read satisfies i < to_read; after the scan is exhausted, run the existing error handling.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: allocation length, scan index, access order, and error return form a clear local fix relationship without proving real attack reachability. original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
Before entering the loop, the code checks the relationship between the initial s and maxbuf and performs a one-byte ND_TCHECK2. The loop body also checks the current position, but then advances s by the current byte value plus one. The next while (*s) directly reads the new position before the loop body can protect it; if the advancement goes beyond the readable range, an out-of-bounds read may occur. The old checks cover only the position before advancement.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read: after pointer advancement, the loop condition dereferences the new position before the boundary check
original_descriptions.security_change:
The only difference is to add ND_TCHECK2(*s, 1) after s += (*s) + 1, checking the new position's single byte before the next loop condition reads it. Under the expected semantics that the macro checks readability and enters truncation handling on failure, the check returns -1 and blocks this out-of-bounds read.
Current review fix mechanism description: A check of the old cursor cannot protect a new cursor advanced by a length byte. After advancing, validate the range needed by the first dereference of the new cursor and exit on failure before the loop condition reads it.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the same loop has a clear check-order fix and the local relationship can be marked as passing. This depends on ND_TCHECK2's ordinary boundary-check semantics; its macro definition is not provided, so exact bounds cannot be determined. after still does not recheck s < maxbuf before the loop condition, so it does not prove that a read beyond maxbuf but still permitted by the macro is solved; the length-driven pointer arithmetic also gains no new range constraint.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
When NE_BUG is false, the import-relocation branch excludes only rel.index > ModRefs and then reads modref[rel.index - 1]. modref is allocated for ModRefs ut16 elements; when rel.index is 0 and this access executes, subtracting one yields an index outside the valid array range. The exact negative or wraparound form depends on an unprovided field type but does not affect the out-of-bounds relationship. Existing allocation and upper-bound checks cannot block zero; the original branch when NE_BUG is true already checks for a positive value and is a different cause.
Current review type description: insufficient lower-bound array-index validation causing an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125)
original_descriptions.security_change:
after removes the conditional-compilation branch at import-module selection: it first maps an index above ModRefs to an unknown module name, then reads modref[rel.index - 1] only when rel.index > 0, so the actual access is constrained by 1 <= rel.index <= ModRefs. It also stores the sequence-name return value in fname and frees it after formatting; whether this fixes a leak depends on the helper's ownership contract. A new #define NE_BUG 0 in the non-additive relocation chain disables the conditional-compilation check immediately following it.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before converting an external one-based number to a zero-based array index, reject values beyond the element count and then require the number to be strictly positive; perform subtraction and dereference only when both bounds hold.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the same import branch, modref object, and index access have a clear local fix relationship and can be marked corrected_passed; the old issue requires NE_BUG false and a zero index reaching the access, without claiming real attack reachability. after retains name as NULL for zero index and still passes it to a name helper or string-formatting function, whose safety depends on an unprovided NULL-argument contract. The ownership contract for fname is also not shown. The non-additive relocation chain still uses only 0xFFFF as normal termination and has no visible cycle detection; these limitations do not negate the index-boundary fix or establish complete safety.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
There are two boundary risks. First, when checking the a= prefix, the code directly reads *(scanner->curptr+1), even if the next character is outside the scan range; it must read it before deciding whether it is '='. Second, after parsing an attribute name, the outer condition checks only the current character before the colon is consumed; if pj_scan_get_char(scanner) consumes ':' and reaches EOF, the inner code still dereferences curptr and may call pj_scan_get_until_chr. The original CR/LF check cannot replace an end-boundary check. Whether the access crosses the allocated object depends on buffer layout and scan-API implementation, which are not provided.
Current review type description: potential out-of-bounds read caused by insufficient scan-boundary validation (CWE-125)
original_descriptions.security_change:
The prefix branch first compares curptr+1 with end; when it reaches or exceeds end, || short-circuiting skips the next-character read, calls error handling, and returns NULL, preventing advancement by two characters. In the attribute-value branch, after optionally consuming the colon, it first calls pj_scan_is_eof; at EOF, && short-circuiting skips the current-character read and value call and instead sets value.ptr to NULL and value.slen to 0.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before a lookahead read, use the end boundary to short-circuit the access; after consuming an optional delimiter, recheck EOF rather than reusing the pre-advancement state, then decide whether to read the attribute value or produce an empty value.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep as a clear local boundary fix: the two changes protect the corresponding prefix read and attribute-value parse path. The analysis assumes end represents the scan end and pj_scan_is_eof accurately reports end; real attack reachability need not be proved. In after, the outer condition still directly dereferences curptr and the first check still forms curptr+1; validity of these operations and safety of the final pj_scan_skip_line depend on scanner constraints not provided, so the whole function is not claimed free of out-of-bounds risk.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
In the branch where new_cursor_col < 0 and State & INSERT holds, ptr points to the current line after indentation adjustment, new_cursor_col is a byte offset, and vcol is the accumulated display column. The loop advances only while vcol <= curwin->w_virtcol and does not use the line-end NUL as a stop condition. If the byte offset reaches the NUL before the target display column ends the loop, the old code still passes that position to lbr_chartabsize; if iteration continues, it advances from the terminator and may pass an address after the line end to character processing, causing an out-of-bounds read. A display-column limit cannot replace a string-byte boundary; concrete access depends on the called function and line-buffer range.
Current review type description: potential out-of-bounds read from string traversal beyond the terminator
original_descriptions.security_change:
The only textual change checks ptr[new_cursor_col] for NUL after advancing new_cursor_col and before calling lbr_chartabsize, exiting the loop when found. This stops scanning on the first arrival at the string terminator, so it no longer computes character width for that position or advances again from the terminator in the next iteration. The fix relates the byte-termination boundary and display-column target as joint traversal constraints.
Current review fix mechanism description: When scanning a string by display width, recognize the terminator after each byte-offset update and before processing the new position, exiting instead of continuing past the string boundary while the display target has not yet been reached.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep as a locally valid fix sample. The check occurs after stepping and cannot cover an anomalous step that skips the terminator; related API implementations are not provided. The later write to new_line[curwin->w_cursor.col] still lacks an explicit copied-string-length check in this function, so this change is not a proof of safety for every path.

On truncated input, *in++ in the loop, repeated-byte comparisons, length markers and extended-length reads, and the final memcpy(out, in, 4) may all read beyond the input range. left represents the decoded length still to generate and outSize represents remaining output capacity; neither represents remaining compressed-input bytes, so the original loop condition, output-capacity check, and final left check cannot protect these input reads.

original_descriptions.security_change:

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
After successful query-name expansion, the old code first advances aptr by len, then calls DNS_QUESTION_TYPE(aptr), and checks QFIXEDSZ only afterward. If zero or one byte remains after the query name, a field read requiring two bytes crosses abuf's alen boundary under the stated semantics. The header-length check covers only the header; successful expansion does not prove that later fields are complete, and the post-check cannot prevent a read already performed. Although the variable is named qclass, the macro actually used is DNS_QUESTION_TYPE.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): insufficient length validation before reading the query-type field
original_descriptions.security_change:
Add alen <= len + HFIXEDSZ + 1 after successful query-name expansion and before advancing aptr or reading the field. Assuming len is the length consumed by the query name and the addition is representable, the condition rejects a packet with fewer than two bytes after the name, sets ARES_EBADRESP through failed, and frees qname. Only after it passes is the query type read, and the existing QFIXEDSZ check still validates the full fixed query portion.
Current review fix mechanism description: After parsing a variable-length prefix, validate remaining space using the prefix-end offset and the next field's required length before moving the pointer and reading; a later check of the entire fixed portion cannot replace a check immediately before the individual read.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local fix clearly moves the field-required boundary check before the read. The two-byte read requirement matches the new threshold, but macro definitions are not provided and are not asserted verified; successful expansion is also assumed to return a valid consumed length and the addition is assumed not to overflow. after does not explicitly handle overflow of this addition; SOA content parsing remains mainly bounded by the packet end and does not explicitly constrain names and integer reads to the current record's rr_len. These issues are outside this fix and do not support claiming after completely safe.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
After processing a sub-block, the code assigns I32(ptr) to advance and directly performs ptr += advance and bytes -= advance. If advance is negative, the cursor may move before the input start and the remaining length increases; if advance exceeds bytes, the cursor may pass beyond the pointer range allowed by the input object. The entry check bytes < 10 constrains only current remaining length and cannot validate this update or reliably protect later reads after the cursor/length relationship is broken. Whether the cursor leaves the allocated object depends on input-buffer range.
Current review type description: unchecked sub-block advance length causes out-of-bounds pointer arithmetic and potential out-of-bounds read
original_descriptions.security_change:
After reading advance and before updating ptr and bytes, reject advance < 0 or advance > bytes, set IMAGING_CODEC_OVERRUN, and return -1. An accepted advance satisfies 0 <= advance <= bytes, so with a valid current cursor and remaining length it preserves the relationship between forward movement and remaining-length decrement. The other change in case 7 only changes a comment's available-byte count from 10 to 4 and does not affect execution.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before synchronously advancing a cursor and decrementing the remaining amount using input-provided length, constrain the length to the closed interval [0, remaining]; report an error and exit first when out of range, then update both values only on the valid path, preventing cursor and length metadata from diverging.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep as a local fix pair: length validation directly controls the original two state updates, so the relationship is clear. It assumes ptr and bytes correctly describe remaining input when reaching the update. This does not establish complete function safety: the check occurs after sub-block processing and cannot protect reads already performed; the COPY branch still copies directly according to state->xsize, and the LC branch still reads *data++. after also does not require advance to cover the sub-block header. ERR_IF_DATA_OOB is not defined, so its exact bounds or exit behavior are not inferred.

original_descriptions.security_change:

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
In the single-quote branch that parses digits after a backslash, the loop checks p[i - 1] and increments i. If the digit sequence extends to the string end and vim_isdigit treats NUL as non-digit, when the loop exits p[i - 1] is NUL but p[i] reads the byte after the terminator. If the terminator is at the end of the readable object, this access is out of bounds. Existing p[1] and p[2] non-NUL checks protect only the parse entry and do not constrain i after digit scanning.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read (byte after the terminating NUL)
original_descriptions.security_change:
In the same single-quote branch's trailing-quote test, first check p[i - 1] != NUL and use && short-circuiting to decide whether to read p[i]. When digit scanning stops at NUL, the code no longer reads the byte after it and does not treat an accidental single quote there as a reason to execute p += i and continue.
Current review fix mechanism description: When scanning uses p[i - 1] as the stopping position but later accesses p[i] forward, first verify that the stopping position is not the terminator and only then perform the forward read; the short-circuit condition blocks both the out-of-bounds read and pointer advancement that depends on it.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local cause and fix correspond directly, exposing a constraint between the scan stopping position and subsequent forward access. The analysis assumes valid NUL-terminated input and that vim_isdigit does not classify NUL as a digit; actual object overrun also depends on readable range after the terminator. after does not change other branches or the final --p; whether this rollback is valid for an empty-string entry depends on caller constraints, so the whole function is not judged safe.

The original len - i minimum-length check constrains logical remaining length, while the common ND_TCHECK(bp[i + optlen]) checks the location determined by the option-length byte; neither directly covers the complete width of this field. original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
Seven mapping-table reads use WC_CCS_INDEX(cc.ccs) - WC_F_ISO_BASE directly as the index. If the character-set index is below the base, the difference may be negative or wrap unsigned, causing an out-of-bounds read; the exact behavior depends on macro and type definitions not provided. The CS94 branch first replaces the ASCII character set with st->g0_ccs, so the replacement must also be constrained. The outer character-set dispatch does not explicitly guarantee this lower bound, and the later if (!g) check occurs after the mapping read and cannot protect it.
Current review type description: array out-of-bounds read: lower bound is not enforced before subtracting the base from the character-set index
original_descriptions.security_change:
Before each of the seven reads that computes an index from the current cc.ccs, after first requires WC_CCS_INDEX(cc.ccs) >= WC_F_ISO_BASE. The check occurs after character-set replacement or conversion and constrains the operand actually used in the subtraction; a value below the base skips the read. g starts at zero, and every visible path that continues iteration does not retain a nonzero g because a nonzero mapping returns from the function. After the skipped read, execution enters the original !g conversion or replacement flow rather than using an invalid index to read the mapping table.
Current review fix mechanism description: For an array index normalized by a base value, after the final modification of the index source, verify that it is not below the base before subtraction and read; preserve the unmapped state on rejection and let the existing fallback path handle it.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep as a clear local lower-bound fix. The conclusion concerns the condition in which the character-set index may be below the base and does not claim real-call reachability or assume macro values, integer widths, or table lengths. after adds no upper-bound check, and the default branch's fixed-difference mapping-table reads are unchanged; their safety cannot be established by this function alone, so after as a whole is not claimed safe.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
When the parser is in PARA_VALUE_QUOTED state and encounters a backslash, the old code directly reads *(tmp+1). The loop condition tmp < end protects only the current character and cannot guarantee that the next character exists; when tmp == end - 1, this read crosses the input interval. If end is the end pointer of the underlying object, this is a memory out-of-bounds read. In addition, after the loop is exhausted, even if the parser remains in a quoted-value state it enters endofheader without explicitly reporting an unclosed quote.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); improperly accepting an argument with an unclosed quote
original_descriptions.security_change:
The backslash branch first checks tmp+1 == end and, when true, jumps to parse_error before the lookahead read and tmp++; tmp still points to the in-range backslash at that point. After natural loop termination, it separately checks PARA_VALUE_QUOTED and sends an unclosed quote to error handling. The added endofheader debug log does not change the boundary relationship. However, when the loop ends with tmp == end, the new error-path log still contains *tmp, leaving a boundary read issue.
Current review fix mechanism description: A loop boundary for the current character cannot replace the boundary check for a lookahead. First verify that the next character remains inside the input interval, then read and skip the escaped character; when input is exhausted, reject an incomplete structure according to parse state, and ensure error reporting also avoids dereferencing an end pointer.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the lookahead read and boundary fix in the same quoted-escape branch correspond clearly, so the local fix can be marked as passing. Assume buffer/end describe the same valid input interval; actual memory overrun depends on whether end is also the readable-object boundary. after is not completely safe: an unclosed quote enters parse_error after loop exhaustion, and if LM_ERR evaluates its character argument it reads *end. External implementations such as add_param are not provided, so no other ownership vulnerability is inferred.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
When entering the outer switch, the old code directly reads buf[0]; with no readable byte, this is out of bounds. When len is 1 and the first byte enters the 0x00, 0xf0, or default branch, it also reads nonexistent buf[1]. The existing len > 5 protects only buf[2] through buf[5] in the 0x7f and 0xbf branches and cannot protect these earlier or other-branch reads. Actual memory out-of-bounds is conditional on the readable range of buf being insufficient.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): instruction-decoding accesses are not constrained by input length
original_descriptions.security_change:
Before reading buf[0], first return -1 when len < 1; then, in the three outer branches that read buf[1], break out of the outer switch when len < 2, avoiding the second-byte access. The existing length protection for six-byte reads remains. The remaining differences are whitespace changes and do not alter expression semantics.
Current review fix mechanism description: Set length thresholds by actual access index: require len >= 1 before the first byte, require len >= 2 after entering a branch needing a second byte, and terminate the path before access when insufficient; higher-index reads remain protected by len > 5.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the same function and buffer accesses have a clear local fix relationship, and the mechanism can be extracted by interpreting len as readable input length. after still sets op->size to 2 and returns when a one-byte input enters a protected branch; some branches may also report an instruction size greater than len. Downstream impact cannot be determined from this function, so these behaviors do not affect the local read fix and do not establish complete safety.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
postcount is decoded from the low nibble and 15 is converted to 16. When postcount > 0, the old code reads postcount bytes from iphc_ptr and writes them to ipaddr->u8[16 - postcount], then advances iphc_ptr. If the packet has fewer remaining valid bytes, this copy crosses the packet-data boundary; whether it also crosses the underlying allocation boundary depends on buffer layout. Existing count limits and zero-padding conditions constrain only address construction and do not guarantee that the source packet has enough data.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): remaining packet length is not validated while decompressing an address suffix
original_descriptions.security_change:
In the same suffix-copy branch, first add the offset of iphc_ptr relative to packetbuf_ptr to postcount and compare it with packetbuf_datalen(). If the required endpoint exceeds packet length, log a warning and return false, blocking that copy and cursor advancement; an endpoint equal to the length is allowed. The return type changes from void to bool, and normal completion returns true.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before reading a source buffer according to a decoded length, validate “current offset + read length <= valid data length”; return first on failure, and copy and advance the cursor only on success while exposing failure through the return value.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local source-read boundary fix relationship is clear. Necessary assumptions are that packetbuf_ptr is the packet start, packetbuf_datalen() is valid-data length, the cursor belongs to the same buffer, and pointer difference and addition are representable. after does not independently verify these prerequisites or the readable length of prefix. The failure check occurs after prefix copying and zero padding, so ipaddr may already be partially modified on a false return; caller handling of failure is not visible. These limits do not negate the local suffix-read check.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
When UIP_TCP is enabled, the old function first reads UIP_IP_BUF->proto and, when it is TCP, reads UIP_TCP_BUF->flags to test SYN. A protocol-number check cannot prove that the packet contains a complete TCP header; if a short packet still satisfies the protocol condition, reading flags may exceed the valid packet range and may start a timer based on invalid data. Whether it exceeds the underlying allocated object cannot be determined from the current source.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds-read risk caused by insufficient packet-length validation
original_descriptions.security_change:
Add uip_len >= UIP_IPTCPH_LEN + uip_ext_len at the beginning of the same condition, relating valid length to the required IP/TCP header length including extension-header length. Under && short-circuit order, insufficient length no longer reads proto or flags or starts the timer; only after length passes does it test TCP protocol and the SYN flag.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before accessing packet-header fields, establish a length threshold from base-header length plus variable extension length and use short-circuit evaluation so the length check precedes field reads and any state operation they trigger.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The loop uses linepos as an index and reads linebuf[linepos++], then checks whether the result is NUL. If no terminating character is encountered within the valid input range and token_len has not reached tokenbuflen, a later iteration may read out of bounds. The existing token_len check limits output tokenbuf length and cannot constrain the input index; this is especially relevant when skipping leading whitespace, because linepos keeps increasing while token_len remains 0.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read from the input buffer (CWE-125)
original_descriptions.security_change:
Add input-length parameter linebuflen and, before every linebuf read, check linepos >= linebuflen and return 0 when true. When input is exhausted, the function now exits before performing an out-of-range read along this path; the existing output-length check and post-read NUL test remain in their original order.
Current review fix mechanism description: Introduce an independent length boundary for input scanning and validate that the cursor is below it before every cursor-based input access. Cumulative output length cannot replace input bounds, especially when a branch consumes input without increasing output length.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The non-null s is used as both start and end. The old code scans byte by byte first toward the lower address and then toward the higher address until a newline; if no newline exists within the valid storage range in the relevant direction, it may read out of bounds. The only !s check excludes a null pointer and does not constrain the scan range. After two unconditional increments, the scan result is used directly to calculate del_lump's offset and length; the concrete consequence depends on that API, whose implementation is not provided.
Current review type description: potential out-of-bounds read from an unbounded newline scan; the fix still has boundary-handling defects
original_descriptions.security_change:
Add a stream parameter, constrain the backward condition to start > stream->body.s, and constrain the forward condition to end < stream->body.s + stream->body.len. Assuming the start belongs to that range and pointer arithmetic is valid, scanning stops moving at the boundary instead of relying only on newline termination. However, the left side of && dereferences first and the right side checks the boundary afterward, and the post-loop start++ and end++ remain unchanged, so the fix does not fully protect boundary reads or the deletion range.
Current review fix mechanism description: Bind a delimiter-terminated bidirectional scan to the same object's lower and upper bounds so every pointer move is range-constrained. This sample also shows that the boundary test must precede dereference and should distinguish delimiter termination from boundary termination, avoiding unconditional increments that corrupt the final range.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep; the local fix relationship is clear: the corresponding stream body bounds are introduced into the same scan branch. This assumes stream is valid, s lies within the relevant object, and pointer comparison and arithmetic are valid; the source does not validate these conditions. If body.s + body.len is a non-readable end pointer, after still reads it first; end++ may then form a deletion endpoint beyond the body. When backward scanning terminates at the lower bound, start++ skips the first body byte. Passing here only means the local scan-range restriction can be extracted and does not mean after is fully safe.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The 0xfb branch continuously reads buf[3] through buf[6] with oa=3, combines delta, and computes op->jump. Entry checks reject only len < 1, which protects buf[0] but not the maximum index 6; setting op->size = 7 does not validate input length. When len denotes readable byte count and is 1 through 6, this branch reads beyond the input range; if the actual buffer contains only those bytes, it is an out-of-bounds memory read.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125)
original_descriptions.security_change:
Place the unconditional shifted reads and jump-target calculation in the 0xfb branch under len > 6. First confirm that at least 7 bytes are available, then read buf[3..6] and update op->jump; when shorter, skip the entire read block and block the same out-of-bounds-read path.
Current review fix mechanism description: Bind execution of a read block to the maximum access index: the maximum index is oa + 3 = 6, so require len > 6 before reading operands and calculating output that depends on them.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the same branch, buffer, and read operation have a clear local fix relationship, assuming len denotes buf's readable length. When length is insufficient, after still sets CALL type, size = 7, and fail and does not assign jump on this path; subsequent effects cannot be determined from this function. In addition, the 0x11 through 0x19 and 0x1e branches still read buf[1] without a len >= 2 guard, so the whole function is not claimed free of out-of-bounds risk.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The ordinary-label branch copies label_len bytes from packet + j to cp. When the length byte is readable and destination space is sufficient but the label content has fewer than label_len bytes, memcpy reads outside the packet range specified by length. GET8 guarantees only that the length byte is read with j < length; the label_len <= 63 limit constrains one label's length, and cp + label_len < end protects destination space, but neither proves that the source label content is complete. The next-loop check occurs after the copy and cannot prevent this read.
Current review type description: CWE-125: source-buffer out-of-bounds read while copying a label
original_descriptions.security_change:
In the same ordinary-label branch, after the destination-space check and before memcpy, a check for j + label_len > length returns failure, requiring the source-label range to lie wholly within the packet range before copying and advancing the cursor. The removed j >= length loop-entry check is covered by the immediately following GET8 check with the same condition, and the failure path still returns -1.
Current review fix mechanism description: After reading a length field, do not treat readability of the field itself or sufficient destination capacity as evidence that the source content is complete; before copying, verify that source start plus copy length does not exceed the input boundary, then copy and advance the cursor.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: both sides are complete and the local repair relationship is clear, extracting a mechanism that validates the source range and destination capacity separately before copying. The conclusion assumes that length correctly describes the readable packet range, the initial index is nonnegative, and the relevant pointers and integer operations are valid; it does not assume that the caller guarantees these conditions. after still does not check whether the initial *idx is negative, and the signed addition j + label_len is not explicitly protected against overflow; this pass addresses only the local out-of-bounds read caused by truncated label content.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The original loop evaluates *data first and checks i < length afterward; when the remaining length is zero, or after traversing length nonzero bytes, it still reads a byte outside the declared range. In the EGRESS_VLAN_NAME branch, even when length is zero it reads the label, advances data, and decrements length, causing an unsigned-length underflow for u_int; later loops may continue reading beyond the original attribute range. The definition of the entry macro ND_TCHECK2(data[0],length) is not provided; even if it checks readability over the specified length, that does not establish safety for a read beyond the range or that a zero-length attribute contains label bytes. Actual physical out-of-bounds behavior depends on buffer bounds and macro behavior.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); unsigned-length underflow expands the read range (CWE-191)
original_descriptions.security_change:
The EGRESS_VLAN_NAME branch now requires length >= 1 before reading the label, advancing the pointer, or decrementing the length; otherwise it jumps to trunc, blocking zero-length reads and the length underflow. The loop is changed to test i < length first, using && short-circuit evaluation to stop when the length is exhausted instead of reading *data first. Two other insufficient-length print-and-return paths are changed to jump to the common trunc path; they do not change the location or condition of the checks.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before consuming a fixed-size field, verify that the remaining length is sufficient, then advance the pointer and decrement the length consistently; while traversing, first verify that the index remains within the remaining range, then read the current byte and check the terminator.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the two local repairs correspond clearly to a minimum-length constraint before label consumption and a remaining-length constraint before loop reads, with no need to prove attack reachability. The boundary analysis treats length as the current number of remaining bytes in the attribute, consistent with pointer advancement and length decrement in the code. In after, the shared TUNNEL_CLIENT_END and related branch still evaluates *data before the length < 1 check; the zero-length read issue is not solved there, so the entire function cannot be considered safe.

The loop assigns *ptr to answer.rname and then passes &answer to pico_dns_record_decompress; that call may change answer.rname. original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The old code returns only when tl1 > l2; otherwise it compares at most tl1 bytes with strncmp(tstr1, str2, tl1). If l2 permits that length but the actual readable data in str2 is shorter than tl1, and the comparison does not end at a null character or differing character before the boundary, str2 may be read out of bounds. tl1 <= l2 establishes only a parameter-length relationship and cannot by itself prove that actual data is sufficient.
Current review type description: conditional out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): comparison length is not constrained by the actual captured-data boundary
original_descriptions.security_change:
after adds an ndo parameter and first uses ND_TTEST2(*str2, tl1) to check the tl1-byte range beginning at str2; failure returns 0. It then still checks tl1 <= l2 and calls strncmp only after that. Under the captured-boundary-check semantics expressed by the macro name and accompanying comment, this places the actual captured-range constraint before comparison and blocks the truncated-data read path described above.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before a read with a length limit, constrain the requested length and logical length together with the actually available data range; first verify that the target buffer covers the complete requested range, return on failure, and then perform the original length check and comparison.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The old code confirms only that shm_ref obtains a non-null mem->mobj, then copies rmem->offs and rmem->size and returns success without relating these operands to object capacity. Even when the object exists, the offset plus length may exceed mem->mobj->size or overflow during addition. This function does not directly access the memory range; a later access using these parameters without another check may go out of bounds.
Current review type description: insufficient shared-memory parameter-range validation, potentially causing a later out-of-bounds access
original_descriptions.security_change:
After copying the offset and length, a checked sum using ADD_OVERFLOW(mem->offs, mem->size, &req_size) is added; if overflow is reported, TEE_ERROR_SECURITY is returned immediately. Otherwise, the interval end req_size is compared with mem->mobj->size, and an end beyond object capacity also returns an error; success is returned only after both checks pass.
Current review fix mechanism description: After obtaining a valid object, perform a checked addition on the read offset and length, then compare the non-overflowing interval end with that object's capacity; reject every failure before returning success instead of accepting external interval parameters merely because the object exists.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The loop reads ts->buffer[i+188] and ts->buffer[i+192] while looking for later synchronization bytes. Assuming buffer_size is the number of valid bytes and the additions do not wrap, the original condition i+188 > buffer_size allows i+188 == buffer_size; when buffer[i] == 0x47, the following read is outside the valid range. If the 188-byte probe does not find a match, the 192-byte probe continues, but the original check does not ensure i+192 < buffer_size and may also read out of bounds. The while condition guarantees only that the current position i is in range and cannot protect these two lookahead positions.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read: off-by-one boundary and larger offset in lookahead probing are not protected
original_descriptions.security_change:
The exit condition before the 188-byte probe is changed first to i+188 >= buffer_size, excluding an index equal to the end; after the 188-byte probe misses, execution exits on i+192 >= buffer_size before the 192-byte probe. original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The old loop uses only num_params as its bound and first reads saved_attr[n]; after the attribute matches TMEM or the RMEM branch is enabled by CFG_CORE_DYN_SHM, it then reads param->u[n].mem.mobj and passes it to mobj_put. If num_params exceeds the valid capacity of the corresponding array, an out-of-bounds read may occur. The attribute branch filters only the parameter kind; it cannot protect the earlier saved_attr[n] read or ensure that the param->u[n] index is valid. The further effect of an invalid pointer on mobj_put cannot be determined from the supplied source.
Current review type description: conditional out-of-bounds array read, potentially passing an invalid object pointer to reference cleanup
original_descriptions.security_change:
The only change replaces the loop bound num_params with MIN((unsigned int)TEE_NUM_PARAMS, num_params). Under the semantics of MIN taking the smaller value, the loop excludes an index that reaches the parameter limit before reading the attribute, so the same upper bound constrains the object-pointer read and cleanup call in the matching branch as well.
Current review fix mechanism description: Bound traversal by the smaller of the requested count and supported capacity, applying the boundary before the first indexed read so subsequent resource cleanup selected by attributes shares the same index bound.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local repair relationship is clear and can be extracted as limiting the requested count to the parameter-capacity bound before indexed access. original_descriptions.security_change:

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
pixnum is obtained by adding pixels_set and offset, and yi is pixnum/image_width. The old code checks only the screen x-coordinate xs and then directly reads row_pointers[yi] to test whether it is NULL. If yi exceeds the valid row-pointer-array range, the null check itself is an out-of-bounds read; if the result is non-null and the palette index is valid, the row pointer is then used to write RGB or RGBA bytes. The x-coordinate and palette checks cannot bound yi, and the null check cannot prove that its own index is valid.
Current review type description: row-pointer-array index out of bounds, potentially causing an out-of-bounds pixel write
original_descriptions.security_change:
after restores the calculation ys=image_top+yi and, before the first row_pointers[yi] read, checks yi<image_height, xs<screen_width, and ys<screen_height in sequence. The new image-height check first rejects a yi outside the logical image rows, and the screen-height check rejects an out-of-range computed y coordinate; only then are the original row-pointer NULL check, palette read, and pixel write executed.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before using a derived row number to access a pointer table, bound the row by image height and then bound the offset-adjusted y coordinate by screen height; only after the boundary checks pass read the table entry, test for null, and write pixels.

In the !(t1 & 0x80) branch, code_length starts as t1 & 0x1f. Whenever code is less than the current mincode_table entry, the old code increments code_length and then reads mincode_table at the new value. After the loop exits, it also reads maxcode_table at that value. If the comparison continues until the index passes the table boundary, an out-of-bounds read may occur. The recursion-depth limit does not constrain the table index; the bitsleft check occurs after the table access, and index_count constrains later symbol_offsets access, so neither protects these lookups.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The cache is allocated for num_chunks pointers, so a valid index should be less than num_chunks. The old check rejects only chunk_num > num_chunks and allows equality; when the cache is available, the subsequent chunk_cache[chunk_num] first reads the element just past the array. If that read does not cause an early return and later allocation, reading, and signature verification succeed, the function finally writes buf to the same out-of-bounds location. Allocation-failure handling and later signature checks cannot protect the earlier cache access.
Current review type description: off-by-one boundary check causing an out-of-bounds cache read and potentially write (CWE-193, CWE-125, CWE-787)
original_descriptions.security_change:
The only textual change replaces the entry comparison > with >=. An equal-boundary value now returns NULL before cache allocation, lookup, and write-back, so an index passing the check satisfies chunk_num < num_chunks and the after-the-end access above is blocked; when num_chunks is zero, chunk_num zero is rejected as well.
Current review fix mechanism description: Treat the element count as an exclusive upper bound and reject index >= count before any array access, making the entry's allowed range agree with the index range of the array allocated for count elements.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: cache allocation count, index operation, and entry bound directly form a clear local repair relationship, without needing to prove actual call reachability. The analysis assumes that cache capacity agrees with num_chunks and that allocation-size calculation is correct. after does not check allocation size or the arithmetic range of the location expression within this function, nor confirm that chunk_size is at least 4 before accessing buf[0..3]; whether these are guaranteed externally cannot be confirmed from the input, so no additional vulnerability or complete after safety is asserted.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
before selects a branch based only on ipv4_hdr->proto and then reads the TCP/UDP dport and sport, or the ICMP type and code, from f->transport_hdr. If the corresponding fields extend past the end of the frame buffer, an out-of-bounds read occurs; the protocol check does not prove that the field's memory is readable, and clearing temp does not protect these source-memory accesses.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read (transport-layer header fields)
original_descriptions.security_change:
Before the protocol branches, after compares f->transport_hdr + sizeof(struct pico_trans) with f->buffer + f->buffer_len and reads transport-layer fields only when the former does not exceed the latter. When the boundary condition fails, both protocol branches and the temp.proto assignment are skipped, leaving the ports and proto zeroed, and ipfilter_apply_filter is still called; this modification skips parsing rather than directly dropping the frame.
Current review fix mechanism description: First verify that the end of the header to be parsed does not exceed the buffer end, and only then enter the protocol branch to read fields; on failure, retain the initialized state and continue later processing. The checked structure size must cover the fields actually read, and the pointer origin and arithmetic must be valid.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: TCP/UDP field reads and the new upper-bound condition have a clear local repair relationship. This interpretation assumes that the pointer arithmetic represents buffer positions as intended, buffer_len describes the valid range, and transport_hdr is already within the buffer; the input does not provide these member types or call constraints. after does not check the lower bound of transport_hdr, and IPv4-field reads still have no local length protection. The ICMP branch uses sizeof(struct pico_trans) as its threshold; whether it covers type and code requires the structure definition, so all header accesses cannot be declared safe from this evidence.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
When processing a non-starting line, pos comes from columnPos(l, col), and the end position is computed as pos + ecol - col. The old code directly writes parentheses to l->lineBuf[pos - 1] and l->lineBuf[a->end.pos], and modifies the propBuf range [pos, a->end.pos). If pos < 1, the left-parenthesis index may be negative; if the end position reaches or exceeds the current line's valid boundary, the right-parenthesis write may be out of bounds. Existing protection only filters anchors, confirms that the line exists, and skips the starting line; it does not relate the column span from source line ls to the storage bounds of target line l.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds array write: lower and upper bounds of line-buffer indices are unconstrained
original_descriptions.security_change:
After computing the end position and before writing to either buffer, a new pos < 1 || a->end.pos >= l->size check skips the remaining operations for the current line when true. This directly blocks an insufficient left start and an end position at or beyond size; when the end is not less than pos, arithmetic does not overflow, and size represents the buffer boundary, it also constrains the subsequent property-modification range.
Current review fix mechanism description: Relate the target-line write position derived from a source-line column span to the target-line boundary before modifying the actual buffer; skip the current iteration's write whenever either checked boundary is not satisfied.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local boundary-repair relationship is clear. The out-of-bounds judgment assumes that l->size represents the relevant storage boundary; the input does not define the buffer capacity. after does not explicitly check that the end position is nonnegative, that the end is ordered relative to pos, or that position calculation does not overflow, so all index cases cannot be declared safe. The check also occurs after putAnchor and anchor-field assignments; skipping buffer modification does not undo those anchor operations.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
Both failure branches of jsmn_parse read dat->chain to produce diagnostic text. The original parser.pos > 10 protects only the copy start parser.pos - 10; copying 20 bytes from there also requires at least 10 bytes after parser.pos. When the position is still within the input but fewer than 10 bytes remain at the end, memcpy crosses the boundary represented by dat->size. err[20] = 0 terminates only the destination string and cannot protect the source read. The other branch outputs a fixed precision of 10 starting at parser.pos; if logging has printf semantics, fewer than 10 bytes remain, and there were no earlier zero bytes, it may also read out of bounds. Actual memory overrun depends on the buffer's readable range.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read in an error-diagnostic path (CWE-125)
original_descriptions.security_change:
Both failure branches first compute remaining = dat->size - parser.pos, and execute the original 20-byte copy only when parser.pos > 10 and remaining > 10; otherwise, the diagnostic string's precision is changed to remaining. When the position is valid and the difference is representable by int, the copy window lies within the input range and the fallback output is constrained by the actual remaining length. remaining > 10 is stricter than the remaining >= 10 actually required by the copy. Error return and release of tokens.tokens after the second parse failure remain unchanged.
Current review fix mechanism description: Diagnostic paths also need source-object boundary constraints: first calculate the remaining amount from input length and current position, then constrain both ends of a fixed window; when the window is not valid, use the remaining amount to limit fallback-string reads instead of a fixed output length.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local boundary repairs for the two corresponding operations are clear and can be extracted as length constraints on error-diagnostic reads. The necessary assumptions are that dat->size is the readable input length, parser.pos lies in that range, the remaining length is exactly representable by int, and logging supports the format-string semantics used. after does not explicitly validate the position range or whether the difference is representable when converted to int; if remaining is negative, printf-style string precision does not provide the intended upper bound. These boundaries are not fully guaranteed within this function, so after is not declared completely safe.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
When rdp->rc4_decrypt_key is NULL at entry and decrypt_use_count < 4096, the old code directly passes the empty context to crypto_rc4, processes data in place for length bytes, increments both counters, and returns TRUE. The original count threshold determines only whether to update the key and does not ensure that the context is valid. Whether crypto_rc4 dereferences a null pointer depends on its implementation, which is not provided.
Current review type description: use of a null RC4 context; may cause a null pointer dereference
original_descriptions.security_change:
rdp->rc4_decrypt_key is checked before the count-threshold test and all key operations; if empty, FALSE is returned immediately. An empty context therefore does not continue to the update branch or decryption call, and the counters are not incremented or success reported.
Current review fix mechanism description: Validate the entry context before using object state; return on failure and block later processing and success-state updates. This check covers only the entry value; a context assigned later in the update branch requires a separate validity guarantee.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the rejection path for an empty entry context and its relationship to the original decryption call are directly visible, enough to establish the local repair. The null-pointer consequence remains conditional on crypto_rc4 requiring a non-null context. after does not check the return value of crypto_rc4_init in the update branch; if that call can return NULL, the entry check cannot protect later use of the new context. The source also does not check whether rdp itself is NULL, and its call constraint is unknown.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The top-level type == 4 branch uses the input unsigned len as its bound and repeatedly performs avio_r8(pb) and hexadecimal logging. If the declared length is large but the data ends early, the old loop does not exit based on EOF status. original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
After calling lvm_set_type, the old code unconditionally copies sizeof(*op) bytes to &p->code[p->end] and then increments p->end. If insufficient space remains in the destination buffer, memcpy writes out of bounds. The function neither checks the write range nor handles lvm_set_type's failure result; even if that call protects its own write, it does not establish that the subsequent operand write has enough space.
Current review type description: bytecode-buffer out-of-bounds write (CWE-787)
original_descriptions.security_change:
The return type is changed from void to lvm_status_t. The result of lvm_set_type is saved first; if it is not LVM_TRUE, the function returns immediately, preventing the operand write. On success, the updated p->end is checked with p->end + sizeof(*op); when it reaches or exceeds DB_VM_BYTECODE_SIZE, LVM_STACK_OVERFLOW is returned. Only after this check does the function execute memcpy, advance p->end, and return LVM_TRUE. This boundary rule also rejects a write that would exactly reach the capacity limit.
Current review fix mechanism description: For a staged append operation, first propagate failure from the preceding step, then check capacity using the write offset after that step and the pending length; return before copying and advancing the offset on failure, and commit the later data only on success.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local repair relationship is clear. The capacity protection assumes DB_VM_BYTECODE_SIZE is the valid capacity of code, p->end is a valid nonnegative offset, and the addition does not wrap; the input does not provide the relevant types or layout, so these conditions are not established universally. after does not explicitly prevent wraparound in the boundary calculation; the capacity check occurs after lvm_set_type, and no explicit rollback is shown for state that call may have changed before an overflow return. These limits do not affect extraction of the pre-write capacity constraint and failure short-circuit mechanism.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
count comes from the input and controls the marker loop. For a positive, large count after conversion, if the input is exhausted early, the read functions return, and execution can continue, before still repeatedly reads marker fields, processes names, and calls avpriv_new_chapter until i reaches count. The original i < count limits only the declared item count and does not ensure that corresponding input exists; sizeof(name) limits the name output buffer and cannot prevent repeated processing after exhaustion. The exact resource-consumption extent depends on external API behavior.

original_descriptions.security_change:
In after, avio_feof(pb) is queried before reading fields on each marker iteration; on EOF it returns AVERROR_INVALIDDATA, so that and later iterations no longer read fields, process names, or call avpriv_new_chapter. The byte-by-byte skip of the header name is also changed to avio_skip(pb, name_len); that change alone does not establish a new length-bound check.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The version == 2 branch reads vst->nb_frames from the input and uses it to loop over pos, asize, and vsize, calling av_add_index_entry separately for audio and video streams. If index data is exhausted early, the old code still performs skipping, index insertion, and timestamp updates and continues to later iterations. The loop bound constrains only the declared frame count and does not ensure that the corresponding records exist in the input; earlier stream allocation, sample-rate, and channel handling also do not check whether index data is exhausted. A large declared frame count may cause many invalid iterations and index operations; exact memory growth depends on index-API behavior, and the source is insufficient to establish an out-of-bounds access.
Current review type description: continuing to build an index for the declared frame count after input exhaustion, potentially causing excessive resource consumption (denial of service)
original_descriptions.security_change:
The only change checks avio_feof(pb) after reading the three index fields on each iteration. Once input exhaustion is reported, AVERROR_INVALIDDATA is returned before this iteration's avio_skip, the two index insertions, and timestamp update, and later iterations are prevented as well. The loop therefore gains an input-state constraint and no longer relies only on the frame count declared in the header.
Current review fix mechanism description: For a parsing loop driven by an input-declared count, check the exhaustion state after reading record fields and before committing derived indices or updating state; exit on a failed read to avoid continuing for the declared count without a valid record.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: both sides clearly show the local repair for input exhaustion in the same index loop and support passing it; the resource effect is conditional on a large declared frame count and reads reporting exhaustion, without requiring proof of attack reachability. after does not check the input state again after the subsequent avio_skip(pb, 8), so it cannot establish that every record is complete; index-insertion return values are still unchecked. In addition, another version's audio read_table failure branch still returns ret without receiving the result of that call; these issues are outside this repair.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
When output_buf is NULL and num_rows > 0, the first loop iteration must read the row pointer through output_buf[row] before calling jzero_far, causing a null pointer dereference. The original row < num_rows condition limits only the number of rows processed and does not ensure that the output row-pointer array exists; even when width is 0, it cannot protect evaluation of this argument. Later code also obtains output_ptr from the same array and accumulates pixel output.
Current review type description: null pointer dereference (CWE-476)
original_descriptions.security_change:
Before the row loop, a new output_buf == NULL && num_rows check calls ERREXIT(cinfo, JERR_BAD_PARAM) when it matches. If that error handling prevents continuation, an empty output array is rejected before the first output_buf[row] evaluation. num_rows equal to 0 still skips the loop; a negative value also triggers the new error even though the original loop would process no rows.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before indexing an output-pointer array by row, bind the state requiring row processing to a non-null-array requirement and terminate the invalid path through error handling before the first access.

original_descriptions.security_change:

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
On entering the sprop-parameter-sets branch, the old code directly reads value[strlen(value) - 1] to test whether the string ends with a comma. If value is a valid empty string, strlen returns 0, unsigned subtraction by one wraps, and the resulting index does not refer to a valid character in the string, causing an out-of-bounds read. The original comma test necessarily performs this read first and cannot protect an empty string; the length check in the profile-level-id branch does not cover this path.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read caused by subtracting one from the length of an empty string
original_descriptions.security_change:
Before accessing the final character, *value == 0 is added and || short-circuit evaluation is used: an empty string goes directly to the warning and return path, without calculating length minus one or reading the final character, and without clearing extradata_size, freeing extradata, or calling the parameter-set parser. A non-empty string continues with the original trailing-comma test.
Current review fix mechanism description: Check for an empty string before reading its final character, using short-circuit evaluation so that length - 1 is calculated and used only when the length is at least 1; reject invalid input before later state changes.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the complete text directly confirms the local repair relationship in the same branch between empty-string out-of-bounds read and early rejection, without needing to prove actual call reachability. The analysis assumes that value points to a valid NUL-terminated string; after does not handle a null pointer or a missing terminator, and the input gives no calling constraints for those cases, so overall function safety is not asserted.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
When malloc returns NULL, before still uses data->strval as the destination of memcpy and then executes data->strval[size] = '\0'. With nonzero size, the copy accesses an invalid destination; even when size is zero, the later terminator write accesses memory through a null pointer. The function has no check of the allocation result protecting these operations.
Current review type description: null pointer access caused by an unchecked memory-allocation failure
original_descriptions.security_change:
Immediately after malloc, after checks data->strval. On allocation failure it calls plist_free_data(data), records an error, and returns NULL, so that path cannot continue to the copy, terminator write, or strlen; the successful-allocation path retains the original processing order.
Current review fix mechanism description: Validate a dynamically allocated buffer before later copy and indexed writes; on failure, call cleanup and return so every operation requiring a valid destination occurs only on the successful-allocation path.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local repair relationship between allocation failure and subsequent null-pointer accesses is clear without assuming actual attack reachability. The cleanup function's internal behavior is not provided, so complete resource-release correctness is not asserted. after still does not explicitly validate plist_new_plist_data's result, allocation-length arithmetic and conversion, or that the source buffer has size readable bytes; whether these are issues depends on implementations or input constraints not supplied and does not affect the judgment on this allocation-failure path.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
When stl->error is false and facet_num is negative, the old function still reads neighbor[0..2] through stl->neighbors_start[facet_num]. If neighbors_start points to the start of an array, this index is before the array. The existing error-state check does not constrain facet_num, and the comparison with -1 occurs after the read and cannot protect it. The values read are then used to choose which connection-statistics field to decrement.
Current review type description: potential out-of-bounds read caused by a negative index
original_descriptions.security_change:
The entry return condition adds facet_num < 0. A negative facet index is rejected before any neighbor element is read or statistics field modified, blocking the negative-index access and dependent update; the nonnegative-index path retains the original logic.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before using a signed parameter to index an array, reject negative values and make that check govern the related read and state update that depends on the read.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the negative-index access on the same indexed object and the preceding rejection have a clear local repair relationship. The out-of-bounds judgment assumes neighbors_start points to an array origin intended for nonnegative indexing; the storage layout is not shown. after does not check the upper index bound or pointer validity, so safety of the other paths cannot be inferred from this repair.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
When maxlen > 0, the readable range consists exactly of maxlen scan units, and none contains a zero terminator, the old code reads the maxlen-th nonzero unit, sets len to maxlen, finds that len > maxlen is false, and continues by reading the next unit. The byte branch advances b by 2 and then reads b[0] and b[1]; the ordinary branch dereferences subsequent elements through the next while (*c++) evaluation. The original check can return only after an additional nonzero unit has been read and cannot protect that access. The null check excludes only an empty wstr.
Current review type description: potential out-of-bounds read caused by an off-by-one boundary check (CWE-125)
original_descriptions.security_change:
Both branches change the return condition to len >= maxlen, so after the maxlen-th nonzero unit is read and counted, the function returns immediately and does not read the next unit. In the byte branch, the check remains before b += 2 and the next two-byte read; the ordinary branch uses while (*c) and moves c++ after the check, so pointer advancement is also controlled by the boundary check.
Current review fix mechanism description: After reading and counting the current nonzero unit, exit immediately when the count reaches capacity; advance the pointer and read the next unit only while the count remains below capacity. The boundary must constrain the next read rather than report overflow only after crossing capacity and reading again.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: both sides have a clear local boundary-repair relationship, suitable for corrected_passed. The out-of-bounds conclusion assumes that maxlen denotes the actual number of readable scan units; the definition of BITCODE_TU and call constraints are not provided, so no width for ordinary-branch elements or actual call reachability is asserted. after still reads the first unit before checking the length, so maxlen == 0 does not guarantee zero access; the byte branch's first read still requires at least two readable bytes. This repair does not establish complete function safety.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
before unconditionally reads *s, *(s + 1), and *(s + 2). If s points to an empty string or a one-character string and there is not enough readable storage after the terminator, the later reads cross the object boundary. The later strncmp(..., 3) limits only comparison length and cannot protect the earlier reads from s; the three write indices into month[3] are themselves within bounds.
Current review type description: conditional out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): reading bytes after the terminator of a short string
original_descriptions.security_change:
After generating month[0], after immediately checks whether it is zero and returns when it is, avoiding the read of s[1]; after generating month[1], it performs the same check, avoiding the read of s[2]. Assuming case conversion preserves NUL as zero, the unconditional consecutive reads are changed to read the next character only after confirming that the previous converted character is not the terminator, blocking the short-string overread above.
Current review fix mechanism description: Set a gate in read order: check whether the already read and converted character is the terminator and return before accessing the next offset. This mechanism depends on the conversion result preserving terminator semantics.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local repair relationship on both sides is clear. The conclusion assumes that s points to a valid NUL-terminated string and that xtoupper/xtolower convert NUL to zero; the conversion definitions are not supplied, so this semantic assumption cannot be independently verified. after still first dereferences s, does not handle a null pointer, and does not validate the actual length of a non-string buffer; those are outside the visible scope of this repair.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The old code iterates over the luma width and height maxw and maxh; each horizontal pixel pair shares and consumes one cb/cr sample, and each vertical pair shares one chroma row. Remaining rows still read chroma. Rounding the loops to even dimensions and handling the tail constrain only the luma traversal; the code does not check chroma dimensions or account for the parity offsets x0 and y0. If the chroma buffer is configured for the offset sampling grid, it may contain fewer samples than the old traversal requires. For example, with x0 even, y0 odd, width 2, height 3, and only one chroma sample, the old code consumes that sample on the first row pair and then dereferences cb/cr again on the tail row, causing an out-of-bounds read. The relationship between actual chroma capacity and origin is not provided by the function, so this trigger is an explicit assumption.
Current review type description: chroma-sampling traversal ignores image-origin parity offsets and may cause an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125)
original_descriptions.security_change:
The new code first computes offx and offy and subtracts them from the width and height. When offy is 1, it first converts the top row with a constant chroma value of 0, advancing only the luma and output pointers without reading or advancing cb/cr; it then processes row pairs and the tail according to loopmaxh, blocking the extra read above. Within a row pair, when offx is 1 it first processes the first column without advancing the chroma pointers and then processes the remaining columns according to loopmaxw, reducing chroma consumption under the offset. However, the second row of this first-column branch still reads *cb and *cr, and the tail row still uses maxw, so horizontal-offset handling is incomplete.
Current review fix mechanism description: Subtract the sampling-origin offset from the logical traversal range, process boundary pixels that do not consume chroma first, and then traverse the remaining sampling grid; advance luma and output pointers normally and advance chroma pointers only with actual sampling units. This pattern is clear for the vertical-offset path in this sample, while the horizontal tail still has an omission.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep as a local-repair sample: both sides directly show that the origin offset changes chroma-read timing and traversal range, and the repair relationship for the vertical-offset path is clear without proving actual call reachability. The out-of-bounds conclusion assumes chroma capacity is configured for the offset grid. after still has visible limits: the tail row does not apply offx; the second row of the row-pair first-column branch still reads chroma, inconsistent with the comment that the first column uses zero chroma; when maxw < offx or maxh < offy, unsigned subtraction can wrap. Neither side checks allocation failure, dimension-multiplication overflow, or precision shift range within this function. This conclusion does not declare after completely safe.
