original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
filename is allocated 13 bytes. The old code allows copying 9 nonzero filename bytes and 4 nonzero extension bytes, then still writes the separator dot and final terminator. If neither contains a terminator and both reads and location operations succeed, the filename occupies indices 0–8, the dot index 9, the extension is written at indices 10–13, and the final terminator is written at index 14; the last two writes exceed the allocation. Even with an ordinary 8-byte filename plus terminator, a four-byte unterminated extension makes the final terminator write index 13. The existing read-length checks and per-segment loop bounds do not ensure that the concatenation, dot, and terminator fit within 13 bytes.
Current review type description: heap-buffer out-of-bounds write (CWE-787)
original_descriptions.security_change:
The new code copies the actual read lengths and returns a format error when the filename reaches 9 bytes or the extension reaches 4 bytes without encountering a zero byte. The loop increments fn while copying and, when it normally encounters a terminator, uses fn-- to move back to that terminator so later concatenation overwrites it. Filename rejection occurs before appending the dot, and extension rejection occurs before the final zero is added: under the usual contract that read returns no more than the requested amount, a filename reaching the extension branch has at most 8 bytes, the fourth copied extension byte is at most index 12, and an unterminated extension returns immediately; the normal final terminator is also at most index 12. Location changes from tell plus an absolute position to a relative rewind based on the actual read amount.
Current review fix mechanism description: For fixed-capacity concatenation, constrain each field's valid length separately and reserve space for the separator and final terminator; reject data that reaches a field's read limit without terminating before continuing concatenation, and move the write pointer back to the copied terminator.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: within the same branch, fixed allocation capacity, overlong concatenation operations, and the repaired rejection order are directly visible, giving a clear local repair relationship. The capacity derivation assumes the usual contract that read returns no more than the requested amount and does not assume actual attack reachability. after still accepts a short read below the requested limit with no zero byte; then i == len, the relative location amount is 1, and fn-- causes the next concatenation or terminator write to overwrite the last copied byte. This is a visible terminator-validation omission and does not negate the out-of-bounds-write repair or establish complete after safety.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The TCOS_V3 branch reads a record into buf[256] and filters it using only r > 0 and a first byte of 0xA0. If r is the actual number of bytes read, a one-byte record makes buf[1] outside the valid data for this read. The loop uses only buf[1] from the record to constrain its starting index i and cannot ensure that buf[i + 1], buf[i + 2], or the length-derived location buf[i + 1 + buf[i + 1]] is valid. Truncated or malformed lengths may cause reads of unfilled or stale data; when the derived index reaches 256 or greater, it also crosses the buf object boundary. Passing sizeof(buf) as the read capacity cannot constrain an index calculated later from the contents.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); reads beyond the valid record range
original_descriptions.security_change:
The change affects only three conditions in the same record-parsing branch: first, r < 2 rejects a record lacking a two-byte header; then, before each loop iteration, i + 2 < r is required, placing the label, length, PIN-comparison byte, and the length byte read for loop advancement within the valid record; finally, before reading fbz in the 0x90 branch, the actual derived index i + 1 + buf[i + 1] < r is required. In header, fixed-offset, and length-derived order, the checks cover the original read paths.
Current review fix mechanism description: For parsing a length-encoded record, treat the declared traversal bound and actual valid-byte bound separately: validate the header first, then the maximum fixed offset in the loop body, and finally, after calculating an index from a field length, validate that actual index before dereferencing it.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local repair relationship is clear. The necessary assumption is that a positive return from sc_read_record is the actual number of valid bytes and does not exceed the supplied capacity; its implementation is not provided, so this contract is not treated as verified. after restricts the relevant reads to r but does not verify that the outer declared length agrees with r or that inner fields lie completely within the outer declared range; record-format validation and complete function safety are therefore not established.

If r is the actual number of bytes read, a one-byte record makes buf[1] outside the valid data for this read. The loop uses only buf[1] from the record to constrain its starting index i and cannot ensure that buf[i + 1], buf[i + 2], or the length-derived location buf[i + 1 + buf[i + 1]] is valid. Truncated or malformed lengths may cause reads of unfilled or stale data; when the derived index reaches 256 or greater, it also crosses the buf object boundary. Passing sizeof(buf) as the read capacity cannot constrain an index calculated later from the contents.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); reads beyond the valid record range

required_target_facts.observed_patch_description:
The change affects only three conditions in the same record-parsing branch: first, r < 2 rejects a record lacking a two-byte header; then, before each loop iteration, i + 2 < r is required, placing the label, length, PIN-comparison byte, and the length byte read for loop advancement within the valid record; finally, before reading fbz in the 0x90 branch, the actual derived index i + 1 + buf[i + 1] < r is required. In header, fixed-offset, and length-derived order, the checks cover the original read paths.
Current review fix mechanism description: For parsing a length-encoded record, treat the declared traversal bound and actual valid-byte bound separately: validate the header first, then the maximum fixed offset in the loop body, and finally, after calculating an index from a field length, validate that actual index before dereferencing it.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The old code allows a nonzero plen smaller than sizeof(struct sctp_paramhdr) to enter the parameter branch. The upper-bound check on offset + plen constrains only the declared range, and the size checks for each store constrain only copy length; neither ensures that plen is large enough for the header. If parameter retrieval succeeds and plen is smaller than the corresponding specialized structure size, plen - sizeof(*p_random), plen - sizeof(*hmacs), or plen - sizeof(*chunks) wraps as an unsigned subtraction and is then converted to uint16_t. The anomalous length may drive HMAC/chunk element reads or a later memcpy beyond the parameter data actually obtained; the exact extent depends on structure sizes and parameter-retrieval behavior not provided.
Current review type description: insufficient lower-bound validation of parameter length; conditional unsigned-length wraparound and out-of-bounds read
original_descriptions.security_change:
The only change replaces plen == 0 with plen < sizeof(struct sctp_paramhdr). After reading the type and declared length, a length smaller than the common parameter-header size is rejected before entering the type-specific branch to obtain data, calculate net length, traverse elements, and concatenate the key. Such a short parameter therefore no longer participates in the branch's length subtraction or subsequent accesses. Failure handling remains break, after which key and association state updates after the loop still execute.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before using an externally declared total length to obtain a parameter, subtract the header size, and form a traversal or copy length, first establish that the total is at least the header size; an upper bound on buffer capacity or input range cannot replace this lower-bound relationship. If a specialized header is larger than the common header, its corresponding lower bound is also needed.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep and pass: both sides clearly concern the same parameter-parsing entry and repair the local mechanism by which a nonzero short parameter could pass the lower-bound check, without requiring proof of actual attack reachability. The out-of-bounds consequence is conditional on the retrieval function accepting a short parameter and the anomalous length driving actual access. Specialized structure definitions are not provided, so it cannot be asserted that the common-header lower bound covers every specialized structure; after also does not explicitly handle wraparound in length += offset or offset + plen, and it continues state updates after an anomalous parameter. This conclusion does not establish complete function safety.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
before returns bufPos directly after the loop even if the 0x61 branch was never entered or its parser returned nonnegative while nextPayload.size was not positive, without a local failure decision. The original bufPos < 0 handles only a failure reported by the subparser and does not require user data to exist. Also, while guarantees only bufPos < endPos before reading a tag; if the tag is the last byte, incrementing bufPos makes it equal endPos, yet the length decoder is still called. Whether an actual out-of-bounds read occurs depends on the decoder implementation not provided, so memory overrun is not asserted.
Current review type description: insufficient input validation: parsing may accept a result with no valid user data; insufficient boundary protection before length decoding
original_descriptions.security_change:
after initializes hasUserData to false; it sets it to true only when the subparser in the 0x61 branch returns nonnegative and self->nextPayload.size > 0. At loop end, if it remains false, -1 is returned, rejecting a result in which the condition was not observed. Separately, after reading a tag and before calling the length decoder, bufPos == endPos is checked, directly rejecting input with no remaining length byte.
Current review fix mechanism description: Bind the acceptance condition for required content to the parse result in the corresponding tag branch and validate it once before successful return; after advancing the cursor past a tag, revalidate the input boundary required for the next length decode.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local repair relationships are clear enough to confirm both user-data existence validation and the end-of-tag boundary protection, without assuming the decoder must overread. A limitation is that nextPayload is not cleared at this function's entry, so a positive size denoting new data depends on parseFullyEncodedData updating it; once hasUserData is true it is not cleared by later branches. Therefore final payload validity is not established. The selector's len > 16 check limits only copy-length upper bound, and the source does not explicitly validate remaining source length; its safety still depends on the length decoder and other external semantics.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
In the is_alt branch, the loop reads each 16-byte identifier into specificToolID[i] for num_alternate entries. If the consumed nbBytes plus 16 exceeds DescSize, the old code still performs the read first, then increments the count and exits; an error return after the loop cannot undo a read that already crossed the descriptor boundary. The source establishes a logical-bound violation, while whether the underlying buffer is overrun depends on the read API and actual input length; an out-of-bounds write to the destination array is not asserted.
Current review type description: read beyond the descriptor boundary: length checked only after reading
original_descriptions.security_change:
The post-read check in the same loop is replaced with a pre-read nbBytes + 16 > DescSize check. When less than one complete identifier remains in the descriptor, GF_ODF_INVALID_DESCRIPTOR is returned immediately, so that read and count advance do not occur; exactly 16 remaining bytes are still accepted.
Current review fix mechanism description: For a fixed-length read in a loop, compare consumed bytes plus the current read length with the current object's length boundary; reject an over-bound operation before any read side effect instead of discovering the error afterward through an accumulated count.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: both sides clearly change the same read from after-the-fact reporting to a pre-read boundary constraint, so the local repair relationship holds. The analysis interprets DescSize as descriptor length and nbBytes as consumed bytes according to their code use, without requiring actual attack reachability. after still reads the fixed header and fallback count fields before checking them; the URL branch also does not check that s bytes are within the remaining descriptor space before reading, and allocation results are unchecked. original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The detailed parsing path directly computes len-sizeof(struct eigrp_common_header) without first ensuring that len is large enough; a short length can make tlen an incorrect large remaining length. Although TLV parsing requires the header size <= eigrp_tlv_len <= tlen and calls ND_TCHECK2 over the declared TLV range, it does not ensure that the payload contains the fields of the selected type. For example, when a GENERAL_PARM payload is empty or shorter than the fields read, holdtime and k1 through k5 are still read beyond the TLV's declared boundary; if those reads also exceed actual readable data, a buffer out-of-bounds read occurs. The IP branch's plen <= 32 limits copy length to the capacity of prefix[4] only and does not by itself ensure that the plen field or copy source is readable.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read caused by inconsistent TLV length and field-read range (CWE-125); underflow risk when subtracting the packet-header length (CWE-191)
original_descriptions.security_change:
Before calculating tlen, after rejects input whose len is smaller than the common-header size. It retains the original total-TLV-length check and range check, and in the GENERAL_PARM, SW_VERSION, IP_INT, IP_EXT, AT_CABLE_SETUP, AT_INT, and AT_EXT branches it compares tlv_tlen with the corresponding structure's sizeof before reading fields; if insufficient, it breaks out of the switch and blocks decoding that branch. A second added TLV-header-size check is already covered by the earlier return with the same condition and is redundant rather than an independent repair.
Current review fix mechanism description: First validate that total length is sufficient to subtract a fixed header, then compute the remaining length; for a payload interpreted by type, relate the declared payload length to the size of the object being decoded and exit a short-payload branch before field access. Capture range, protocol-object bounds, and destination capacity for copies should be validated separately.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local repair relationship is clear, separately constraining the remaining-length subtraction and type-field reads by the corresponding length boundary. No specific structure size or actual attack reachability is assumed; the exact effect of capture protection depends on the ND_TCHECK macro definition not provided. after still does not explicitly ensure tlen is at least the header size before reading the TLV header; an invalid-TLV branch still passes a pointer after the header and an unadjusted tlen to print_unknown_data, and any overread depends on that function's implementation. The storage range of the IP destination is not given, so the sizeof check cannot be shown to cover every byte_length byte. The common-header length check also has not been moved before initial header-field reads or the non-detailed path. Only the stated local repair is accepted; after is not declared comprehensively safe.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The old code reads the byte at buf offset 4 and writes it directly to if_descriptor->bNumEndpoints. If the input endpoint count exceeds USBH_MAX_NUM_ENDPOINTS, the field retains the input value. If later code traverses endpoint storage whose capacity is limited by that bound, an out-of-bounds access may occur, but the supplied code does not show such use.

original_descriptions.security_change:
The only change applies MIN to the input count and USBH_MAX_NUM_ENDPOINTS before writing bNumEndpoints. Under MIN's smaller-value semantics, an over-limit count is first clamped to the limit and then stored in the descriptor field, blocking propagation of a value above the limit through that field. The change does not alter the read offset from buf or validate buffer length.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before parsing an external count and writing it to an internal descriptor field, limit it to the implementation-supported maximum so an over-limit value cannot pass through that field to later processing.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep as a clear local endpoint-count-clamping repair. The necessary assumptions are that MIN returns the smaller value and USBH_MAX_NUM_ENDPOINTS denotes the available endpoint-count limit; its definition is not provided, so concrete storage capacity or actual out-of-bounds reachability is not asserted. after still directly reads buf offsets 0 through 8 without visible length or pointer-validity checks, and that safety must be supplied by the calling context.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
In the id == 26 branch where vendor lookup succeeds, the code overwrites the already checked outer len with the vendor's internal length field, then subtracts vendor->tag + vendor->len and also subtracts the vendor-header overhead from n. The old len >= 0 and 2 + len <= n checks occur before these changes and cannot constrain the new operands. If the internal length is smaller than the internal-header overhead, the new len is negative; if too large, the payload may extend beyond the remaining received data. When dictionary lookup finds a non-array string property, this len is then used for _malloc(len + 1), memcpy, and the terminator index; a negative len passed to memcpy converts to an unsigned length, while a large positive len can read past the received data. Even when the property is not matched, later ptr += len and n -= 2 + len use the unreviewed length and break the relationship between the parse cursor and remaining bytes. Whether execution crosses an allocated-object boundary depends on buffer capacity and path.
Current review type description: vendor-attribute length is not revalidated after recomputation, potentially causing out-of-bounds reads and a negative length to participate in memory operations
original_descriptions.security_change:
After recomputing the vendor-internal length and remaining bytes, and before dictionary-property lookup and payload handling, after first rejects len < 0 and then rejects 2 + len > n. At this point n still includes the two-byte outer-attribute header, so the second constraint says that the payload length after ptr cannot exceed n - 2. Either failure jumps to out_err, frees pack, and returns, preventing an invalid recomputed length from reaching later copies, indexing, and cursor updates.
Current review fix mechanism description: In nested-format parsing, an outer length check cannot be reused after an internal field overwrites the length; after subtracting the internal header and synchronizing the remaining amount, revalidate that payload length is nonnegative and no greater than the current remainder before accessing payload or advancing the cursor.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local repair relationship is clear; the memory-operation risk is conditional on vendor and property dictionary matching and entering the corresponding type branch, with no need to assume specific dictionary contents. after still reads the vendor ID, tag, and length before the new check; the loop also reads an ordinary attribute header before confirming that two bytes remain. The new check constrains only the remaining received data, does not preserve the outer attribute length to bound the internal property, and does not address iteration by received length rather than pack->len, destination-field capacity, or the minimum IPv6-prefix length checks visible in the source. Overall function safety is not established.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The loop requires only total_subobj_len > 0 and then reads two header bytes from obj_tptr + offset. Later length checks constrain the declared subobject length but do not prove that the capture buffer contains the fields to be read. In the exchange-type branch, the code reads offsets +2 and +3 before checking the four-byte range at offset +4; that check is both after the earlier reads and does not cover the four-byte maximum-bandwidth field at offset +8. The wavelength branch directly reads the four-byte field at offset +4. When captured data is insufficient and the corresponding read executes, an out-of-bounds read risk exists.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): incomplete capture-boundary protection before reading subobject fields
original_descriptions.security_change:
Five ND_TCHECK calls are added: the first checks the two header bytes before type and length are extracted; in the exchange-type branch, corresponding ranges are checked before each one-byte read at offsets +2 and +3 and before the four-byte read at offset +8, while the existing check at offset +4 is retained; in the wavelength branch, the corresponding range is checked before the four-byte read at offset +4. Under the semantics of ND_TCHECK checking capture bounds and routing failure to trunc, truncated input returns -1 before the corresponding field read.
Current review fix mechanism description: Treat declared length and actual readable range separately; before extracting the header and fields in each branch, check the range from the same base with the relevant offset and read width, rather than letting an earlier field check cover later fields or checking only after the read.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local repair relationship is clear. The judgment assumes ND_TCHECK performs a capture-boundary check as indicated by its name and existing trunc structure; its definition is not provided, so no implementation is inferred. after still does not verify that the declared length for each type is sufficient for its fields: the exchange branch needs at least 12 bytes and the wavelength branch at least 8, while the generic check permits length 4; with sufficient capture data, a field may still be read beyond the declared subobject. The loop also does not ensure total_subobj_len >= 2 before reading the two-byte header. This pass covers only the added capture-boundary protection.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
size comes from the received packet header. before initializes the stream using c->in_s->size but receives data into c->in_s->data with the unconstrained length size - 8; if the requested length exceeds actual capacity and the receive interface does not protect separately, an out-of-bounds write may occur. When size < 8, the subtraction cannot represent a valid payload length, and the exact wraparound or conversion depends on types and interface definitions not supplied. For size 8 through 11, the payload is shorter than the two 16-bit fields, yet after successful reception the code may continue parsing beyond the valid packet range. Version checks, receive-result checks, and the first-field command-set check do not establish a relationship among size, receive capacity, and the length required by the two fields.
Current review type description: insufficient packet-length validation causes mismatch among receive length, buffer, and required parse length, with out-of-bounds read/write risk
original_descriptions.security_change:
after first requires the total length to be at least 12 and no greater than SCP_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE; failure returns immediately, preventing an invalid length from reaching subtraction, payload reception, and field parsing. original_descriptions.security_change:

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The encrypted-sample branch uses sai->IV_size as the read length for gf_bs_read_data and sai->IV as the destination. This length is filled by sample-information lookup or set to 16 when there is no trak. The old code checks only that the length is nonzero; if it exceeds the actual capacity of IV and the read function writes the requested length, an out-of-bounds write may occur. The later check for fewer than 6 bytes of remaining input protects only reading the subsample record, occurs after the IV read, and does not constrain the IV destination capacity.
Current review type description: potential out-of-bounds write caused by an unconstrained destination-buffer boundary
original_descriptions.security_change:
Before the IV read in the same encrypted-sample branch, a check for sai->IV_size > ARRAY_LENGTH(sai->IV) is added. On overflow, the current sai is first passed to the cleanup function and GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE is returned, so that IV read does not execute and the current sai is not added to the list; a length within the bound retains the original nonzero-length read.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before using an externally derived length to write to a destination, compare the length with destination capacity; on overflow, clean up the current object before it enters the container and return, so rejection precedes the dangerous access.

The interpretation depends on ARRAY_LENGTH(sai->IV) denoting a valid capacity in units consistent with the read length; field types, macro definition, and read API implementation are not supplied, so concrete capacity or actual attack reachability is not asserted. after does not explicitly check that sufficient input exists for the IV, and the paths that memset after allocation or return directly after sample-information lookup failure remain unchanged; those issues are not solved by this repair.

On overflow, the current sai is first passed to the cleanup function and GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE is returned, so that IV read does not execute and the current sai is not added to the list; a length within the bound retains the original nonzero-length read.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before using an externally derived length to write to a destination, compare the length with destination capacity; on overflow, clean up the current object before it enters the container and return, so rejection precedes the dangerous access.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
After entering the MPLS extension branch, the old code calls in_cksum with the start ext_dp->icmp_ext_version_res and length plen - ICMP_EXTD_MINLEN: icmp_length is zero when probing the extension and is also used for outputting the checksum when the version is supported. If the extension header is readable but the capture does not cover that length, checksum calculation may read out of bounds. ND_TCHECK(*ext_dp) checks the fixed object and cannot ensure coverage of the entire checksum range determined by plen; the lower-bound condition on plen likewise does not establish sufficient captured data. The earlier ND_TTEST2 for whole-packet checksum controls only its own branch and, after failure, extension processing may still be entered.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): MPLS extension checksum uses a length without validated capture bounds
original_descriptions.security_change:
The two extension checksum calculations each add an ND_TTEST2 condition corresponding to vec[0].ptr and vec[0].len. The code first validates the plen - ICMP_EXTD_MINLEN byte range beginning at icmp_ext_version_res, then sets the checksum vector and calls in_cksum. If the first test fails, extension-probe checksum is skipped; if the second fails, output of the checksum result is skipped. Neither directly exits later parsing.
Current review fix mechanism description: For an operation that traverses data by a packet-declared length, check capture bounds using the actual read start and complete read length, and let the successful check govern each read call; a fixed-header check or a check in another branch cannot substitute for this condition.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the two changes clearly correspond to the same checksum-range out-of-bounds-read mechanism and establish a local repair relationship. The judgment assumes ND_TTEST2 expresses a capture-boundary test and in_cksum reads according to the vector length; no implementation or structure layout is inferred. after is not a proof of overall safety: object parsing still compares hlen with obj_tlen only after processing the data, and the tag read has no explicit requirement that the object payload contain at least four bytes; these length relationships are not addressed by this change.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The shared branch for PUBACK, PUBREC, PUBREL, PUBCOMP, and SUBACK calls getu16 with p directly and writes the result to mm->message_id. If the declared remaining length is 0 or 1, the original integrity check may still pass: it verifies only that the declared packet body has been received and does not ensure that the two bytes needed by this field lie within [p, end). The read may therefore cross into the next packet; if the actual readable storage is also insufficient, an out-of-bounds read may occur. The implementation of getu16 is not provided; the two-byte-read interpretation is supported by checks before other calls in the same function and by the later p += 2.
Current review type description: read beyond the packet boundary; under getu16(p)'s two-byte-read semantics, potentially a buffer out-of-bounds read (CWE-125)
original_descriptions.security_change:
Before calling getu16, the shared branch checks end - p < 2 and returns a format error when insufficient, blocking a short packet from field reading; after a successful read, p is advanced by two bytes. The receive boundary is also represented as eop and pointer comparison replaces length comparison; this rewrite alone does not establish that other vulnerabilities are removed.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before parsing a fixed-width field, validate its width from the current cursor p to the current packet end end; exit immediately when insufficient and read and advance only when sufficient. Checking that the receive buffer contains the declared packet cannot replace a field-level packet-boundary check.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local repair relationship for the same field read in the same branch is clear and passes without proving actual attack reachability. The necessary assumption is that getu16 reads two bytes under this call pattern. after still computes p + len before validating the declared length, which may create pointer-arithmetic risk beyond the underlying array; length decoding also performs a shift before checking len_len, whose safety depends on integer width and input. The scanto implementation is not provided, so related branches are not declared safe.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The old code stores len + 1 in int nsiz and then rounds capacity, comparing only the derived nsiz with MAX_ARRAY_LIST without independently constraining the original len. If arithmetic or integer conversion makes nsiz unable to represent the requested capacity and the upper-bound check does not reject it, len >= obj->arrMaxSize can still enter the growth branch: allocation uses nsiz, then zeroing begins at the old-capacity position for nsiz - obj->arrMaxSize bytes, potentially producing an invalid address or byte count; arrCnt may then also be updated with a len that was not independently validated. The assert checks only the array flag, and the growth condition compares requested length with old capacity; neither guarantees that calculated capacity covers the request and old capacity. Exact integer behavior and memory consequences depend on types, macro values, and allocation behavior not provided.
Current review type description: array-capacity integer-calculation risk and insufficient length-bound validation may make allocated capacity and zeroing range inconsistent
original_descriptions.security_change:
nsiz and mod are changed from int to uint; the rejection condition changes from nsiz > MAX_ARRAY_LIST to len >= interp->maxArrayList or nsiz > interp->maxArrayList. The new logic constrains both the original request and rounded capacity and returns before reallocation, zeroing, and arrCnt update. original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
When ONIG_SYN_OP_ESC_BRACE_INTERVAL is enabled, the function first checks PEND and then uses PFETCH(c) to read a candidate closing character. If that character is an escape at the end of the input, the old code verifies only that it equals MC_ESC(env->syntax) and then executes PFETCH(c) again. The earlier PEND check occurred before consuming the escape and cannot ensure that input remains for the second read; the digit-range check does not protect it either. If PFETCH does not handle input end itself, the second read may cross end.
Current review type description: potential out-of-bounds read caused by a missing input-end boundary check
original_descriptions.security_change:
The only diff adds || PEND to the escape-character match condition. After the first PFETCH consumes the escape, the code rechecks whether the input has ended; if it has, it jumps to invalid and blocks the second PFETCH. Only when input remains does it read and validate the right brace. The invalid path returns 1 or an error code according to syn_allow and does not perform later token filling or update *src.
Current review fix mechanism description: When consecutive reads are separated by a cursor-advancing read, revalidate the input boundary using the updated cursor before the later read; an initial non-empty check cannot cover the next access after input is consumed.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local repair relationship of rechecking the input boundary after consuming the escape in the same branch is clear. The read risk is conditional on PEND representing input end and PFETCH consuming input without safely handling end itself; macro definitions are not provided, so no read width or actual attack reachability is asserted. after visibly blocks the second read triggered by a trailing escape, but this alone does not prove other accesses such as multibyte decoding are safe.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
When processing three construction or destruction array sections, buf is allocated according to sec->size. The 32-bit branch reads 4 bytes from buf + i each time, while the other branches read 8 bytes, but the old loop requires only i < sec->size. When the section length is not a multiple of the corresponding step and allocation succeeds, the final read crosses the allocation boundary. The allocation-failure check confirms only that the buffer exists; checking that the address is nonzero after the read cannot protect an access that has already occurred.
Current review type description: heap-buffer out-of-bounds read (CWE-125)
original_descriptions.security_change:
The two loop conditions are changed to (i + 3) < sec->size and (i + 7) < sec->size, respectively. Assuming the index arithmetic does not overflow, the code first confirms that the last byte of the current entry remains within the buffer and only then decodes and appends the entry, skipping tails shorter than 4 or 8 bytes.
Current review fix mechanism description: For fixed-step parsing of a buffer, the loop-admission condition must cover the entire entry rather than only its starting offset; decode only after confirming that the last byte lies within the allocated range. This boundary expression also depends on representable index arithmetic.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep and pass: the boundary repair relationship for the two fixed-width reads on the same buffer is clear. The analysis uses the semantics of r_read_le32 and r_read_le64 reading 4 and 8 bytes, respectively; their implementations are not provided. after still uses an int index; for a sufficiently large section, incrementing the index may cause signed overflow, and the current text gives no size upper bound. In addition, both sides ignore the return value of r_buf_read_at, so complete-read status is not validated within this function; these issues do not negate the local repair of the tail out-of-bounds read.

The count read from f is written to gradient->NumGradients. When the count exceeds 8, the old code prints a diagnostic only; exit is commented out, and it still loops using the original count, passing &gradient->GradientRecords[i] to the record parser. The loop can therefore process records at index 8 and above; if the array capacity is the source-implied limit of 8, it exceeds the valid element range. The array definition and called-function implementation are not provided, so actual capacity or exact read/write behavior cannot be confirmed.
Current review type description: array out-of-bounds access risk caused by an input count not being constrained by the valid upper bound
original_descriptions.security_change:
In the same branch for a count greater than 8, gradient->NumGradients is set to 8 before the loop that uses this field as its termination bound. An over-limit input is therefore truncated before a record-element address is formed or the parser is called, and the loop processes at most indices 0 through 7.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before using an input count to index a record array, truncate an over-limit count to the permitted maximum and make subsequent loops use the corrected count directly.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The three strncat calls treat bufSize as the maximum number of characters to append rather than the total destination capacity. If buf has capacity bufSize and the existing string length is L, appending k characters requires L+k+1 bytes; the old code limits only k <= bufSize and cannot ensure that the write and terminating NUL fit. At the first device-name append, even with L=0, a source string of length bufSize makes the terminator out of bounds; later space and type appends also need to subtract existing content. The flags and infoStr conditions control only whether appending occurs and do not guarantee capacity.
Current review type description: destination-buffer out-of-bounds write: append length does not account for existing content and terminator space
original_descriptions.security_change:
Before the first append, buf[0]=0 is set, and the device-name append limit is changed to bufSize-1 to reserve space for the terminator. The subsequent space and type appends each compute bufSize-(strlen(buf)+1) at that point, basing the remaining allowance on the string length formed by the previous step. When bufSize>0, buf has corresponding capacity, and strlen(buf)<bufSize before each append, appended characters and the terminator are constrained by remaining capacity.
Current review fix mechanism description: Maintain the string-append budget in execution order: reserve one terminator byte for the initial empty-string append, and for later appends use total capacity minus current length minus one; every intermediate write must preserve the premise that string length is less than capacity.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local repair relationship is clear and supports corrected_passed, without requiring external macro values or actual attack reachability. The conclusion depends on a valid buffer and the stated capacity conditions. after still unconditionally writes buf[0] and does not handle zero capacity, for which bufSize-1 also underflows; the device-number branch still calls itostr without passing remaining capacity, and its implementation is not provided, so boundedness cannot be confirmed. If that step breaks string bounds, later strlen and subtraction cannot restore safety.

When s->edge_emu_buffer is empty, the old code allocates a buffer of 9 * FFABS(s->current_frame.f->linesize[0]) but continues parsing and later rendering even when the allocation returns a null pointer. The outer condition establishes only that allocation is needed; the earlier check of ff_thread_get_ext_buffer's return value concerns current_frame and cannot ensure that this separate allocation succeeds. This function does not directly dereference edge_emu_buffer, so whether a later null-pointer access occurs depends on called functions not shown and is not treated as a confirmed crash.
Current review type description: unchecked memory-allocation failure (may cause a later null pointer dereference)
original_descriptions.security_change:
Immediately after the same allocation assignment, the new code checks s->edge_emu_buffer; when empty, it sets ret to AVERROR(ENOMEM) and jumps to error, preventing this call from continuing into parsing, rendering, and output. The error path reports current_frame progress and, when the existing thread condition holds, unreferences the current frame before returning the error.
Current review fix mechanism description: For a deferred allocation resource stored in decoder state, validate the result after assignment and before any later processing; on failure, set an explicit error code and enter the existing error path so an invalid resource state cannot propagate.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The query loop passes bufpos directly to _skip_hostname; if the cursor has reached or passed buf + len at the start of an iteration, calling that function may read the current position out of bounds. The answer branch obtains addrlen from the packet; the old check limits only the source-data end, after which a record passing type and class filters is copied with memcpy(addr_out, bufpos, addrlen). Even with sufficient source data, an addrlen larger than destination capacity causes an out-of-bounds write; destination capacity and helper implementation are not provided, so these consequences are conditional.
Current review type description: insufficient DNS-parse boundary control; conditional out-of-bounds read and destination-buffer overflow risk
original_descriptions.security_change:
The query loop now first compares bufpos with the packet end; when it reaches or passes the end, -EBADMSG is returned and that iteration does not call _skip_hostname. In the answer branch, after obtaining addrlen, values greater than SOCK_DNS_MAX_ADDR_LEN are rejected before the cursor moves, source boundary is checked, and records are filtered; copying occurs only afterward, limiting the length passed to memcpy. The source-end check also changes > to >=, additionally rejecting data that ends exactly at the packet end; for memcpy's half-open range, equality alone was not an out-of-bounds read.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before a parsing call, verify that the current cursor has not exhausted the input; compare the packet-declared length with an independent upper bound before allowing the copy. Available source length and destination capacity are different constraints, so the former cannot replace the latter.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep and pass local repair review: the query-cursor check and copy-length upper bound both take effect before their corresponding operations. original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The Image Separator branch checks only whether x+w or y+h exceeds the canvas dimensions. With nonnegative dimensions and representable additions, x == g->w with w == 0, or y == g->h with h == 0, can still pass the original checks (the other axis must also pass). These coordinates are then stored in g->start_x/start_y and g->cur_x/cur_y; if the color-table branch succeeds, they are passed to gif_process_raster. The starting point is already outside the valid canvas coordinate range, but whether raster processing actually reads or writes out of bounds depends on the implementation not provided.
Current review type description: insufficient image-start-coordinate boundary validation; potentially passes an out-of-range coordinate to raster processing
original_descriptions.security_change:
Before the existing right and bottom boundary checks, after adds x>=g->w and y>=g->h tests, constraining each starting coordinate to be strictly less than the canvas dimension. On a match, a runtime error is set and control jumps to end, terminating the branch before image-coordinate state is updated or raster processing is called and blocking propagation of the boundary starting point above.
Current review fix mechanism description: Validate separately that the start lies in the half-open valid coordinate interval and that the endpoint does not exceed the dimension upper bound; checking only start plus length cannot exclude a start at the upper bound when length is zero. Reject the input before persisting coordinate state and passing it to later processing.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the tightened start-bound repair relationship is clear and does not depend on proving an actual out-of-bounds access. The zero-size boundary example assumes the value is representable, the other-axis check passes, and addition does not overflow. after still does not explicitly exclude an in-canvas start with zero width or height and adds no negative-value or addition-overflow protection; whether those cases are possible and their consequences cannot be determined from the supplied read functions and type information, so no additional vulnerability or complete after safety is asserted.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
Each iteration writes four bytes to out[j] through out[j+3], including branches with only one or two input bytes remaining. The entry check compares outSize with inSize * 4 / 3; without arithmetic overflow, this integer expression is still smaller than the 4 * ceil(inSize / 3) needed for padded output. For example, with inSize=1 and outSize=1, the entry check passes and the padding==2 branch writes out[0..3]; if the output object actually has only the declared one-byte capacity, an out-of-bounds write occurs.
Current review type description: output-buffer out-of-bounds write (CWE-787): capacity estimate does not cover four-byte tail padding
original_descriptions.security_change:
The only change returns 0 in each iteration after computing padding and before all output branches when j+4>=outSize. Assuming the addition does not overflow, the four-byte write occurs only when j+4<outSize, blocking the same output access when remaining capacity is insufficient. This check is stricter than the required j+4<=outSize and also rejects a buffer that exactly fits the current output.
Current review fix mechanism description: Strengthen an overall capacity estimate with a per-iteration pre-write boundary check: using the current output offset j and fixed write size 4, check the output boundary first and only then enter either a tail-padding or full-group branch. The boundary expression itself must still avoid overflow, and insufficient capacity must be distinguished from exact sufficiency.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: a small input directly shows that the old capacity estimate and actual write range disagree, and the new check blocks that error before a write in the same iteration, establishing a local repair relationship. The out-of-bounds example assumes the output object's actual capacity equals outSize. after still retains arithmetic expressions such as inSize * 4 and j+4 without explicit overflow protection; the specific risk depends on types and values not provided, so all sizes cannot be declared safe. Exact-sufficient capacity is also rejected, and earlier writes are not undone when a later iteration returns 0.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The non-block replacement loop first reads n and enters character replacement when n != NUL. In the single-byte TAB path it then calls coladvance_force(getviscol()), but directly writes PBYTE(curwin->w_cursor, c) without rereading the current position. If that operation, with coladd involved in positioning, moves the cursor to the line-ending NUL, the old check establishes only that a character existed before movement and cannot protect the write after movement; non-NUL c may overwrite the string terminator, allowing later terminator-dependent reads to go out of bounds. The old virtual_op branch uses else if and likewise cannot handle reaching NUL only after entering the character branch.
Current review type description: overwriting the line-terminating NUL, potentially causing an out-of-bounds read
original_descriptions.security_change:
The repair sets done = FALSE at the start of each iteration and sets it to TRUE after a multibyte replacement or completed single-byte write. After TAB positioning and endpoint recomputation, it calls gchar_cursor() again and executes PBYTE only when the current position is not NUL. An independent !done condition then enters end-of-line virtual-space handling: it first extends space by virtual end column plus 1, adjusts the cursor, and replaces characters one by one. This both prevents a write based on the pre-movement state from overwriting the current terminator and gives an unprocessed virtual position the existing expansion handling, while already processed characters are not replaced twice.
Current review fix mechanism description: A position change invalidates an earlier content check; recheck the terminator boundary at the final write location, skip writing a terminator, and use a per-iteration completion flag to route an unprocessed position through expansion-before-write handling.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
Decoding first checks key < table->nentries and reads the corresponding entry, but while walking back through the prefix chain it excludes only entry.prefix == 0xFFF and then directly reads table->entries[entry.prefix]. If the prefix is not the terminator and is greater than or equal to the valid entry count, the access leaves the valid dictionary range; if it also exceeds the underlying allocation, a physical out-of-bounds read occurs. Checking the initial key cannot constrain the prefixes of later entries.
Current review type description: prefix-chain index exceeds the valid dictionary range and may cause an out-of-bounds read
original_descriptions.security_change:
The only diff expands the termination condition before dereferencing the prefix to entry.prefix == 0xFFF || entry.prefix >= table->nentries. Each iteration still outputs the current entry's suffix first and then checks the prefix; an invalid prefix exits the loop and is no longer used to read the next entry, blocking invalid-index access along this prefix-backtracking path.
Current review fix mechanism description: When traversing an index chain, validating the entry point cannot replace validation at every hop; before using a link field from each entry as an array index, recognize the terminator and check the current valid-entry upper bound, then dereference.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: before and after concern the same prefix-chain read and have a clear local repair relationship. The trigger is a dictionary entry containing a non-terminator prefix outside the valid range; its construction path and allocation capacity are not shown, so actual input reachability or a physical overrun on every instance is not asserted. after performs the protection after writing the current frame and does not validate frame write address, entry length, or frame-size arithmetic, so complete function safety is not established.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
When width < w (w=8) or height < h, the corresponding width-w or height-h can be negative; when compared with explicitly unsigned ix or iy, the negative value converts to a large unsigned value and may incorrectly make need_emu false. If no other fallback condition holds and h > 0, edge simulation is skipped and the code reads directly from the offset original src. Each MMX movd reads four bytes, and the two horizontal iterations plus adjacent-row and column operations require a sampling region of width w+1 and height h+1. The original comparison detects right and lower neighboring-sample boundaries when dimensions are sufficient but may fail when dimensions are too small; the reads then exceed the declared image range and may exceed allocated storage if the underlying allocation lacks enough padding. The temporary-buffer constraints for h and stride are also gated by need_emu and cannot correct this false negative.
Current review type description: signed/unsigned comparison invalidates a boundary check and may cause an out-of-bounds read
original_descriptions.security_change:
The original coordinate comparison is extended with width < w and height < h, forcing need_emu when either image dimension is smaller than the processing block. The code then checks whether h or stride needed for edge simulation exceeds the fixed-buffer limit: on excess it calls ff_gmc_c and returns; otherwise it calls ff_emulated_edge_mc_8, points src to edge_buf, and performs MMX sampling. This blocks the path where insufficient dimensions bypass edge handling through unsigned comparison and direct sampling of the original image continues.
Current review fix mechanism description: When a boundary check compares an unsigned coordinate with “object size minus operation span,” also identify the case where object size is smaller than the span, preventing a negative difference from becoming a large unsigned threshold. Include this size relationship in the edge-handling state and, before actual reads, perform the buffer-capacity fallback check followed by source replacement.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local error and repair relationship is clear. The analysis assumes the relevant integer operations are defined and that input can reach the sampling path, without requiring proof of actual call reachability. Whether exceeding the image range becomes an access outside allocated storage depends on actual storage. The two helper implementations are not provided, so their safety cannot be established; after also does not comprehensively validate dimensions, shift range, or pointer-offset arithmetic, and it still computes the original src offset before edge simulation. This conclusion covers only the size-check repair.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
Both paths round the name length up to an 8-byte boundary. The compressed path directly computes len+(8-(len%8)); under the expected unsigned 32-bit mat_uint32_t semantics, a large non-aligned length near the limit can wrap, so later allocation, name read, and nbytes subtraction use a distorted length. Reading and allocation use the same len, so a heap overrun is not directly established. The uncompressed path first stores buf[1] in int name_len, introducing a conversion-range risk; a representable positive length can still overflow signed int during alignment addition and then affect nBytes subtraction and the fseek offset. The existing type and positive-length checks do not bound the alignment addition, and the initial SafeMul check protects only the cell-pointer-array size.
Current review type description: integer overflow and length-conversion risk during name-length alignment (CWE-190)
original_descriptions.security_change:
Before adding for a non-aligned length in the compressed path, the code requires len < UINT32_MAX - 8 + (len % 8), making the aligned result less than UINT32_MAX and leaving room within that numeric domain for the later len+1. The uncompressed path changes name_len to mat_uint32_t and applies the same bound before alignment. On failure, both paths call Mat_VarFree, clear cells[i], and exit the cell loop, preventing the length from driving later allocation, reading, count subtraction, or file positioning.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before rounding an input length upward, calculate the permitted original-length upper bound from the remainder; use one consistent length type so the aligned result and terminator increment are representable. On a bound failure, free the current object, clear the owner slot, and exit the loop so the bad length cannot drive data consumption.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the alignment arithmetic and precondition checks in both name-parsing paths form a clear local repair relationship. The explanation of the exact wraparound range assumes mat_uint32_t is an unsigned 32-bit length type, whose definition is not provided. after still does not verify that name length lies within the remaining matrix data or fully check the representable ranges of nbytes/nBytes and the file-position result; this conclusion does not declare the entire function safe.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
operand starts at 0 and is incremented after each token; the loop first writes initialization fields to op->operands[operand]. The ordinary path checks operand > MAX_OPERANDS only after writing and incrementing, so when operand equals MAX_OPERANDS and another token remains, the next iteration still writes at that index. The shift path increments and immediately continues, completely bypassing the loop-tail check. If MAX_OPERANDS denotes the capacity of operands, these paths write outside the valid index range. Register-number and shift-amount checks constrain field values and cannot protect the array index.
Current review type description: array out-of-bounds write: upper-bound check is late, off by one, and can be bypassed by continue
original_descriptions.security_change:
The diff adds only a pre-access upper-bound check inside the loop: after splitting the token and skipping leading whitespace, operand >= MAX_OPERANDS is rejected before the first op->operands[operand] access. Both the ordinary path and the shift path that continues are routed through this check on their next iteration, so when the index reaches capacity the function returns before writing any array field for that iteration.
Current review fix mechanism description: Place the capacity check before the first indexed access of each iteration and reject index >= capacity; ensure every increment path, including one that continues early, passes through the same check before its next access.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep and pass local repair review. The necessary assumption is that MAX_OPERANDS denotes the capacity of operands; the input does not provide its definition or the ArmOp layout, so concrete capacity or memory location is not asserted. Both sides are sufficient to establish the repair of check position, boundary, and continue coverage. The new error return in after does not free t obtained by strdup, creating a leak path; the existing early returns for excessive shift amount or register number likewise do not free t. The pass covers only array-index protection and does not represent complete after safety.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
When FEAT_EVAL is enabled, execution enters the expression-replacement branch, and copy is nonzero, the old code checks only that eval_result[nested] is non-null and then copies it to dest. For a result of length L, string data plus terminator needs L+1 storage units; if dest has actual capacity destlen and L >= destlen, the copy exceeds capacity. Entry null checks, nesting-depth checks, and the cached-result handling do not establish a relationship between result length and this destination capacity; capacity checks in the ordinary-character and matched-reference branches do not cover this copy.
Current review type description: destination-buffer out-of-bounds write: expression-result copy does not check capacity
original_descriptions.security_change:
The only change adds STRLEN(eval_result[nested]) < destlen after the same cached-result non-null check; only after the condition succeeds does the code copy in order, advance dst, and clean the cache. Assuming destlen is a valid positive capacity and the length comparison behaves as intended, strict less-than reserves one position for the terminator and blocks the whole-result copy when it is too long. If the condition fails, all three operations are skipped, dst remains dest, and the function writes NUL at the end.
Current review fix mechanism description: Before consuming a cached string, relate the current length of the same object to the current destination capacity and use a strict-less boundary that accommodates the terminator; perform copy and cache consumption only when this relationship holds.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local repair relationship between the copy operation and capacity constraint is clear, without needing to prove that a caller actually passes an undersized buffer. The conclusion assumes a valid string, destlen correctly represents destination capacity, and the string-length macro behaves as required here; no macro expansion or concrete type width is inferred. after does not verify that destlen is positive, and the function still writes NUL at the end when copy is nonzero, so a zero-capacity destination is not solved by this condition; the effect of a negative capacity comparison also cannot be determined without macro definitions. When the length check fails, the cache is not cleaned in this branch, and later lifetime effects cannot be determined from this function. Other branch boundaries are unchanged, so overall function safety is not asserted.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The outer while confirms only at the start of each compressed instruction that pbSrc < pbEnd. ExtractRunLength followed by pbSrc += advance, or advancing the pointer after reading pixels, can exhaust the source; the old code then still reads a pixel or dereferences *pbSrc. A directly visible example is the non-SET FGBG_IMAGE branch: if the instruction header consumes the remaining input and runLength > 0, the later bit-mask read accesses the input end. Destination-capacity checks and return-value checks for write functions concern output and cannot protect these source reads.
Current review type description: source-buffer out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), local boundary repair
original_descriptions.security_change:
The diff shows six added pbSrc >= pbEnd checks: before the FG_RUN foreground-color read, before each of the two pixel reads in a dither run, before the COLOR_RUN pixel read, after parsing the FGBG_IMAGE header, and before each expansion read in COLOR_IMAGE. A failed check immediately returns FALSE, blocking the corresponding read when the source pointer has reached or passed the end; the dither run's second check occurs after advancing past the first pixel, and the color-image check repeats per iteration.
Current review fix mechanism description: A variable-length header parse or payload consumption changes the source pointer, so the boundary conclusion at instruction entry cannot be reused. Revalidate the source range needed by the next actual read after advancement; check every loop consumption separately, because output-capacity validation cannot replace input-range validation.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep and pass local repair review. The pixel-macro read width need not be determined to confirm the relationship: FGBG_IMAGE visibly dereferences *pbSrc, and when header parsing and advancement exactly exhaust input while a bit mask is still needed, the new check exits before that dereference. after still lacks a check before every FGBG_IMAGE bit-mask read; after optional foreground-color or an earlier bit-mask read exhausts input, another dereference may remain. If a pixel macro reads multiple source elements, pbSrc < pbEnd alone also does not guarantee the whole pixel is readable. ExtractRunLength internals, macro definitions, and pointer arithmetic cannot be assessed from the supplied text, so overall safety is not claimed.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
In the MODBUS_FC_WRITE_AND_READ_REGISTERS branch, the read and write addresses are each reduced by start_registers, producing mapping_address and mapping_address_write. The old code repeats the lower-bound check mapping_address < 0 and never checks the write-index lower bound. When quantity and byte-count checks pass, the read interval is valid, mapping_address_write is negative, and the write interval's end does not exceed nb_registers, execution still enters the write loop and uses a negative i to write the request's two-byte values to mb_mapping->tab_registers[i]. A positive write count and upper-bound check do not ensure a nonnegative write start; if tab_registers points to the mapping-array origin, the operation writes before the array.
Current review type description: CWE-129 / CWE-787: the lower-bound check targets the wrong register index and may cause a negative-index out-of-bounds write
original_descriptions.security_change:

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
context->quants is allocated as groups of 10 UINT32 values for context->numQuant groups. After reading tile->quantIdxY, quantIdxCb, and quantIdxCr from the stream, the old code does not verify that an index is less than the group count and continues parsing and submitting a thread task or calling rfx_decode_rgb. Any index greater than or equal to numQuant can therefore travel along this path. The existing nonzero numQuant check, stream-length check, and block-type check do not ensure that the index points to an allocated quantization group. If downstream code directly selects a group with these indices, an out-of-bounds read may occur; the downstream access is not shown in the input.
Current review type description: insufficient quantization-table index-range validation; may cause a downstream out-of-bounds read
original_descriptions.security_change:
After reading the three component quantization indices, the new code compares each in turn with context->numQuant; if any index reaches or exceeds the group count, it sets rc = FALSE and exits the tile loop. The check occurs before parsing the remaining tile fields, submitting a thread task, or synchronous decoding, so the current tile with an invalid index is not submitted for processing by this function, and the existing wait and cleanup path follows.
Current review fix mechanism description: For a table-selection index read from input, use the number of element groups actually allocated and populated as the exclusive upper bound; validate each index before any synchronous or asynchronous consumer uses it, and exit the current path through existing cleanup on failure.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Keep: the local repair clearly establishes an upper-bound relationship between all three quantization indices and the group count, so validation and blocking can be confirmed without assuming the downstream addressing formula. The out-of-bounds consequence remains conditional on downstream use not shown. after does not tighten sub length to blockLen or explicitly constrain the sum of component lengths within the current block; these visible boundary issues are not addressed by this change, and their consequences cannot be determined from the current text alone.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The detailed-decoding branch enters its loop only when nitems > 0 && tlen > 0, then immediately extracts a TLV type and length from tptr; a positive number of remaining bytes does not ensure that a complete TLV header is readable. The public-header ND_TCHECK does not cover the following TLV header, and the value-area ND_TCHECK2 occurs after field extraction and cannot protect the earlier reads. The value-area check uses the packet-supplied vqp_obj_len, neither explicitly constraining it to tlen nor ensuring the length required by fixed-width decoding: when an IP object length is 1 through 3, the code still executes EXTRACT_32BITS(tptr), crossing the declared value area; if captured data is also insufficient, it may cross the capture boundary. The MAC branch likewise does not relate declared length to address length, although the exact reads performed by etheraddr_string are not defined in the input.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read: TLV-header boundaries, packet remaining length, and fixed-width value decoding are inconsistent
original_descriptions.security_change:
tlen changes to u_int consistently with len, and before using public-header fields or subtracting the public-header size the code verifies that the header size does not exceed tlen. Inside the loop it first performs ND_TCHECK on a complete TLV header, then verifies that the header size does not exceed tlen, and only afterward extracts fields and advances the cursor. After the value-area capture check it adds vqp_obj_len <= tlen, then requires the IP length to equal 4 and the MAC length to equal ETHER_ADDR_LEN before calling the corresponding decode operation. Every failure transfers to trunc, so the execution order blocks incomplete-header reads, value processing beyond packet remaining length, and short values entering fixed-width decoding; each length subtraction also receives the corresponding precondition.
Current review fix mechanism description: First verify the readable range and logical remaining length of a complete record header, then read its length fields; for the value area, constrain capture range, packet remaining range, and the width required by the type before decoding and advancing the cursor. Passing a declared length check does not by itself protect a fixed-width access.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Retain and pass local repair review. Both sides directly show the relationship between boundary checks and actual read widths in the same parsing path, especially the mismatch between short IP values and four-byte extraction, without requiring proof of attack reachability. The capture-check semantics of the ND_TCHECK family are inferred from the visible calls and comments; macro implementations, structure layout, the value of ETHER_ADDR_LEN, and the internal behavior of the address-formatting function are not provided, so no additional claims are made. after still ends the loop directly when nitems is not exhausted but tlen is zero and does not report an item-count mismatch; this does not negate the local repair or establish that the function has no other issue.

tlen changes to u_int consistently with len, and before using public-header fields or subtracting the public-header size the code verifies that the header size does not exceed tlen. Inside the loop it first performs ND_TCHECK on a complete TLV header, then verifies that the header size does not exceed tlen, and only afterward extracts fields and advances the cursor. After the value-area capture check it adds vqp_obj_len <= tlen, then requires the IP length to equal 4 and the MAC length to equal ETHER_ADDR_LEN before calling the corresponding decode operation. Every failure transfers to trunc, so the execution order blocks incomplete-header reads, value processing beyond packet remaining length, and short values entering fixed-width decoding; each length subtraction also receives the corresponding precondition.
Current review fix mechanism description: First verify the readable range and logical remaining length of a complete record header, then read its length fields; for the value area, constrain capture range, packet remaining range, and the width required by the type before decoding and advancing the cursor. Passing a declared length check does not by itself protect a fixed-width access.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
In the hostsocket branch, snprintf returns the length required for the complete output, not the number actually written. If that length exceeds the capacity of config.prompt, a later config.prompt+len moves beyond the buffer; sizeof(config.prompt)-len no longer represents valid remaining capacity and may undergo unsigned wraparound. Even if the first output is not truncated, the accumulated snprintf return value while appending the database number may make len exceed capacity, after which appending "> " uses an invalid address and length. The existing snprintf capacity argument limits each individual write but cannot make its return value valid as the offset for the next write. The return semantics of anetFormatAddr are not provided, so the same issue is not asserted for the first formatting in the address branch.
Current review type description: formatting return length misused as a buffer offset, causing a potential out-of-bounds write
original_descriptions.security_change:
after removes accumulation of len and offset writes on the fixed buffer. It instead builds prompt in sequence, appends the database number and prompt suffix, and then calls snprintf once from the start of config.prompt with its full capacity, finally freeing prompt. Even if an intermediate formatted result is long, it can no longer use the returned required length to choose a static-buffer write address or remaining capacity.
Current review fix mechanism description: Replace accumulation of a formatting return length as a fixed-buffer write offset with incremental construction of an intermediate string and one final copy from the destination start using its actual capacity, avoiding confusion between required output length and bytes actually written.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Retain: the hostsocket branch and snprintf's return semantics clearly establish the local repair relationship, without requiring assumptions about anetFormatAddr's return value. Correctness of dynamic construction still depends on normal sds-interface behavior; after's address branch calls strlen(addr), which requires anetFormatAddr to produce a NUL-terminated string within addr's range, and allocation-failure handling is not shown. These limitations do not affect the explicitly removed fixed-buffer offset error.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
Content-Length is parsed by atoi into signed contentlen. In the 'U' branch, if contentlen is -1 and the read returns a positive value, the initial l=0 makes i > contentlen-l true; i is then changed to -1 and buf[i]=0 writes before the allocated buffer. The read length LINESIZE-1 limits only the read and cannot protect the index assigned afterward; the error flag cannot prevent a write that occurs before its check, and the loop's exit check occurs later.
Current review type description: negative-length propagation causes an out-of-bounds write before the start of a heap buffer (CWE-124)
original_descriptions.security_change:
contentlen and accumulated length l change to unsigned, the length is parsed with %u, and values exceeding LINESIZE*1024 are cleared. The 'U' branch marks a zero length as an error, requires l < contentlen before reading, and requests the smaller of the remaining length and LINESIZE-1; it then still clips i by the remaining amount. Initial processing requires at least 9 bytes and a matching prefix, and only the no-error branch writes the terminator, decodes, and writes the file. This moves the remaining-length constraint before the read and blocks the old path where a negative remainder became a write index. The form enctype change is unrelated to directly blocking this out-of-bounds write.
Current review fix mechanism description: Use a consistent nonnegative representation for total and accumulated lengths, verify that accumulated length is less than total before computing the remainder and constraining the read, and write the terminator and process content only after content-length and prefix validation; do not let post hoc clipping turn an untrusted negative length into a memory index.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Retain; the local cause and repair correspond clearly. Trigger analysis is conditional on entering the 'U' branch and the read returning a positive value, without inferring an authentication bypass. The boundary argument assumes the read function honors the supplied length and that LINESIZE and the length-limit calculation and assignment to int i are representable; macro definitions and API implementation are not provided, so after is not claimed fully safe. after still does not check the return value of sscanf and, if the read ends early, does not verify that l equals contentlen; incomplete content may still enter the file-truncation flow.

This moves the remaining-length constraint before the read and blocks the old path where a negative remainder became a write index. The form enctype change is unrelated to directly blocking this out-of-bounds write.

original_descriptions.unsafe_behavior:
The original function directly reads the serial-number field with EXTRACT_16BITS(p) and the flag with *p. If length is less than 2, the two-byte read exceeds the declared packet range; if p's actual readable range is also insufficient, an out-of-bounds read may occur. The original ndo_eflag condition controls only prefix output, and length is used for printing; neither constrains field access. The 0x0fff and 0xc0 masks applied after the read cannot reduce the range required by the read itself.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read (header-field access in a short or truncated packet)
original_descriptions.security_change:
Before reading the fields, the code checks length < 2; on failure it prints a truncation marker and returns, then checks ND_TTEST_16BITS(p) and returns on failure as well. Only after both checks pass does it perform the original serial-number and flag reads, placing the declared-length boundary and the two-byte readability check at p before access.
Current review fix mechanism description: First verify that the logical packet length meets the field width, then verify the actual readable range at the field start; return immediately on either failure so the subsequent two-byte extraction and the single-byte read at the same start are jointly protected.
original_descriptions.keep_reason: Retain: the same function and field reads gain an explicit failure path before access, establishing a clear local repair relationship. The readability protection assumes ND_TTEST_16BITS(p) has the macro contract of checking two readable bytes at p; its definition is not provided, so after cannot be claimed entirely vulnerability-free.
